articleTitle: Erratum to “Bounded Gaps Between Primes of a Special Form”
Products of Small Integers in Residue Classes and Additive Properties of Fermat Quotients
abstract: We show that for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon \gt 0$</tex> and a sufficiently large cube-free <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>, any reduced residue class modulo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex> can be represented as a product of 14 integers from the interval <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[1, q^{1/4\,{\rm e}^{1/2} + \varepsilon }]$</tex>. The length of the interval is at the lower limit of what is possible before the Burgess bound on the smallest quadratic nonresidue is improved. We also consider several variations of this result and give applications to Fermat quotients.

articleTitle: Stability Results for Logarithmic Sobolev and Gagliardo–Nirenberg Inequalities
abstract: This paper is devoted to improvements of functional inequalities based on scalings and written in terms of relative entropies. When scales are taken into account and second moments fixed accordingly, deficit functionals provide explicit stability measurements, that is, bound with explicit constants distances to the manifold of optimal functions. Various results are obtained for the Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality and its Euclidean counterpart, for the Gaussian generalized Poincaré inequalities and for the Gagliardo–Nirenberg inequalities. As a consequence, faster convergence rates in diffusion equations (fast diffusion, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, and porous medium equations) are obtained.

articleTitle: The Covering Radius of Randomly Distributed Points on a Manifold
abstract: We derive fundamental asymptotic results for the expected covering radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho (X_N)$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> points that are randomly and independently distributed with respect to surface measure on a sphere as well as on a class of smooth manifolds. For the unit sphere <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBS}^d \subset {\BBR}^{d+1}$</tex>, we obtain the precise asymptotic that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBE}\rho (X_N)[N/\log N]^{1/d}$</tex> has limit <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[(d+1)\upsilon _{d+1}/\upsilon _d]^{1/d}$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N \to \infty $</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\upsilon _d$</tex> is the volume of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-dimensional unit ball. This proves a recent conjecture of Brauchart et al. as well as extends a result previously known only for the circle. Likewise, we obtain precise asymptotics for the expected covering radius of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> points randomly distributed on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-dimensional ball, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-dimensional cube, as well as on a three-dimensional polyhedron (where the points are independently distributed with respect to volume measure). More generally, we deduce upper and lower bounds for the expected covering radius of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> points that are randomly and independently distributed on a compact metric measure space, provided the measure satisfies certain regularity assumptions.

articleTitle: Inequalities for BMO on α-Trees
abstract: We develop technical tools that enable the use of Bellman functions for BMO defined on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex>-trees, which are structures that generalize dyadic lattices. As applications, we prove the integral John–Nirenberg inequality and an inequality relating <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^1$</tex>- and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-oscillations for BMO on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex>-trees, with explicit constants. When the tree in question is the collection of all dyadic cubes in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {R}^n,$</tex> the inequalities proved are sharp. We also reformulate the John–Nirenberg inequality for the continuous BMO in terms of special martingales generated by BMO functions. The tools presented can be used for any function class that corresponds to a non-convex Bellman domain.

articleTitle: From an Initial Data to a Global Solution of the Non-linear Schrödinger Equation: A Building Process
abstract: The purpose of this work is to construct a continuous map from the homogeneous Besov space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot B^0_{2,4}({{\BBR}}^2)$</tex> in the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {G}$</tex> of initial data in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot B^0_{2,4}({\BBR}^2)$</tex> which gives birth to global solution of the mass critical non-linear Schrödinger equation in the space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^4({\BBR}^{1+2})$</tex>. We use the fact that solutions of scale which are different enough almost do not interact; the main point is that we determine a condition about the size of the scale which depends continuously on the data.

articleTitle: Two-Point Correlation Functions and Universality for the Zeros of Systems of SO(n+1)-invariant Gaussian Random Polynomials
abstract: We study the two-point correlation functions for the zeroes of systems of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SO}(n+1)$</tex>-invariant Gaussian random polynomials on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBRP}^n$</tex> and systems of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Isom}({\BBR}^n)$</tex>-invariant Gaussian analytic functions. Our result reflects the same “repelling”, “neutral”, and “attracting” short-distance asymptotic behavior, depending on the dimension, as was discovered in the complex case by Bleher, Shiffman, and Zelditch. We then prove that the correlation function for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Isom}({\BBR}^n)$</tex>-invariant Gaussian analytic functions is “universal”, describing the scaling limit of the correlation function for the restriction of systems of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SO}(k+1)$</tex>-invariant Gaussian random polynomials to any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^2$</tex> submanifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M \subset {\BBRP}^k$</tex>. This provides a real counterpart to the universality results that were proved in the complex case by Bleher, Shiffman, and Zelditch.

articleTitle: On the Free Boundary Min–Max Geodesics
abstract: Given a Riemannian manifold and a closed submanifold, we find a geodesic segment with free boundary on the given submanifold. This is a corollary of the min–max theory which we develop in this article for the free boundary variational problem. In particular, we develop a modified Birkhoff curve shortening process to achieve a strong “Colding–Minicozzi” type min–max approximation result.

articleTitle: Bilipschitz Invariants for Germs of Holomorphic Foliations
abstract: In this paper, we study bilipschitz equivalences of germs of holomorphic foliations in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\BBC}^2,0)$</tex>. We prove that the algebraic multiplicity of a singularity is invariant by such equivalences. Moreover, for a large class of singularities, we show that the projective holonomy representation is also a bilipschitz invariant.

articleTitle: Riesz Transforms Outside a Convex Obstacle
abstract: The goal of this paper was to develop some basic harmonic analysis tools for the Dirichlet–Laplacian in the exterior domain associated to a smooth convex obstacle in dimensions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq 3$</tex>. Specifically, we will discuss analogues of the Mikhlin Multiplier Theorem, Littlewood–Paley Theory, and Hardy inequalities, culminating in a proof that homogeneous Sobolev norms defined with respect to the Dirichlet and whole-space Laplacians are equivalent for the sharp ranges of integrability exponent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> and regularity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>. Counterexamples are included to show that these results are indeed sharp. In particular, we precisely settle the question of boundedness of Riesz transforms on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^p$</tex>, including the endpoint. The utility of such results in the study of nonlinear partial differential equation (PDE) is that they allow us to deduce important results, such as the fractional product and chain rules for the Dirichlet–Laplacian, directly from the classical Euclidean setting. As an application, we discuss the local well-posedness and stability problems for energy-critical NLS. All the results of this paper play an essential role in the authors' proof of large-data global well-posedness and scattering for the energy-critical NLS in three-dimensional exterior domains; see [29].

articleTitle: Admissible Embeddings of L-Tori and the Essentially Tame Local Langlands Correspondence
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic 0 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> be the general linear group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {GL}_n$</tex> over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>. Bushnell and Henniart described the essentially tame local Langlands correspondence for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(F)$</tex> using admissible characters, with their rectifiers, of tamely ramified elliptic maximal tori of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(F)$</tex>. The main result of this article is to relate these rectifiers to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi $</tex>-data in the theory of endoscopy of Kottwitz, Langlands, and Shelstad. Therefore, we can describe the essentially tame local Langlands correspondence using admissible embeddings of L-tori.

articleTitle: Kähler–Einstein Metrics with Conic Singularities Along Self-Intersecting Divisors
abstract: In this paper, we extend the existence and regularity theorems for Kähler–Einstein metrics having conic singularities along a simple normal crossing divisor to the case of normal crossing divisor, that is, when components of the divisor are allowed to intersect themselves transversely.

articleTitle: Recovering S1-Invariant Metrics on S2 from the Equivariant Spectrum
abstract: We prove an inverse spectral result for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^1$</tex>-invariant metrics on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^2$</tex> based on the so-called asymptotic equivariant spectrum. This is roughly the spectrum together with large weights of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^1$</tex>-action on the eigenspaces. Our result generalizes an inverse spectral result from [6] concerning <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^1$</tex>-invariant metrics on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^2$</tex> which are invariant under the antipodal map. We use higher order terms in the asymptotic expansion of a natural spectral measure associated with the Laplacian and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^1$</tex>-action.

articleTitle: Hölder Singular Metrics on Big Line Bundles and Equidistribution
abstract: We show that normalized currents of integration along the common zeros of random <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>-tuples of sections of powers of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> singular Hermitian big line bundles on a compact Kähler manifold distribute asymptotically to the wedge product of the curvature currents of the metrics. If the Hermitian metrics are Hölder with singularities we also estimate the speed of convergence.

articleTitle: The Large-N Limits of Brownian Motions on 𝔾𝕃N
abstract: We introduce a two-parameter family of diffusion processes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\big (B_{r,s}^N(t)\big )_{t\ge 0}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r,s>0$</tex>, on the general linear group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {GL}_N$</tex> that are Brownian motions with respect to certain natural metrics on the group. At the same time, we introduce a two-parameter family of free It⊚ processes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(b_{r,s}(t))_{t\ge 0}$</tex> in a faithful, tracial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W^\ast $</tex>-probability space, and we prove that the process <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\big (B^N_{r,s}(t)\big )_{t\ge 0}$</tex> converges to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(b_{r,s}(t))_{t\ge 0}$</tex> in noncommutative distribution as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N\to \infty $</tex> for each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r,s>0$</tex>. The processes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(b_{r,s}(t))_{t\ge 0}$</tex> interpolate between the free unitary Brownian motion when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(r,s)=(1,0)$</tex>, and the free multiplicative Brownian motion when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r=s=\frac {1}{2}$</tex>; we thus resolve the open problem of convergence of the Brownian motion on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {GL}_N$</tex> posed by Philippe Biane in 1997.

articleTitle: Purity, Formality, and Arrangement Complements
abstract: We prove a “purity implies formality” statement in the context of the rational homotopy theory of smooth complex algebraic varieties, and apply it to complements of hypersurface arrangements. In particular, we prove that the complement of a toric arrangement is formal. This is analogous to the classical formality theorem for complements of hyperplane arrangements, due to Brieskorn, and generalizes a theorem of De Concini and Procesi.

articleTitle: Annihilation of Cohomology and Strong Generation of Module Categories
abstract: The cohomology annihilator of a noetherian ring that is finitely generated as a module over its center is introduced. Results are established linking the existence of nontrivial cohomology annihilators and the existence of strong generators for the category of finitely generated modules. Exploiting this link, results of Popescu and Roczen, and Wang concerning cohomology annihilators of commutative rings, and also results of Aihara and Takahashi, Keller and Van den Bergh, and Rouquier on strong finite generation of the corresponding bounded derived category, are generalized to cover excellent local rings and also rings essentially of finite type over a field.

articleTitle: Existence of Equivariant Biharmonic Maps
abstract: We consider two compact Riemannian manifolds <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> and a compact Lie group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> that acts on both by isometries. Under certain assumptions on the structure of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> and of the quotient space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M/G$</tex>, we construct equivariant biharmonic maps <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u : M \to N$</tex> with prescribed boundary data.

articleTitle: Fano Varieties in Mori Fibre Spaces
abstract: We show that being a general fibre of a Mori fibre space (MFS) is a rather restrictive condition for a Fano variety. More specifically, we obtain two criteria (one sufficient and one necessary) for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex>-factorial Fano variety with terminal singularities to be realised as a fibre of a Mori fibre space, which turn into a characterisation in the rigid case. We apply our criteria to figure out this property up to dimension 3 and on rational homogeneous spaces. The smooth toric case is studied and an interesting connection with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-semistability is also investigated.

articleTitle: Classification of Non-Kac Compact Quantum Groups of SU(n) Type
Additive Number Theory and Inequalities in Ehrhart Theory
abstract: We introduce a powerful connection between Ehrhart theory and additive number theory, and use it to produce infinitely many new classes of inequalities between the coefficients of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^{*}$</tex>-polynomial of a lattice polytope. This greatly improves upon the three known classes of inequalities, which were proved using techniques from commutative algebra and combinatorics. As an application, we deduce all possible “balanced” inequalities between the coefficients of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^{*}$</tex>-polynomial of a lattice polytope containing an interior lattice point, in dimension at most 6.

articleTitle: Ergodic Optimization of Prevalent Super-continuous Functions
abstract: Given a dynamical system, we say that a performance function has property P if its time averages along orbits are maximized at a periodic orbit. It is conjectured by several authors that for sufficiently hyperbolic dynamical systems, property P should be typical among sufficiently regular performance functions. In this paper we address this problem using a probabilistic notion of typicality that is suitable to infinite dimension: the concept of prevalence as introduced by Hunt, Sauer, and Yorke. For the one-sided shift on two symbols, we prove that property P is prevalent in spaces of functions with a strong modulus of regularity. Our proof uses Haar wavelets to approximate the ergodic optimization problem by a finite-dimensional one, which can be conveniently restated as a maximum cycle mean problem on a de Bruijin graph.

articleTitle: On the Discrete Logarithmic Minkowski Problem
abstract: A new sufficient condition for the existence of a solution for the logarithmic Minkowski problem is established. This new condition contains the one established by Zhu [70] and the discrete case established by Böröczky et al. [7] as two important special cases.

articleTitle: Hilbert Basis Theorem and Finite Generation of Invariants in Symmetric Tensor Categories in Positive Characteristic
abstract: In this paper, we conjecture an extension of the Hilbert basis theorem and the finite generation of invariants to commutative algebras in symmetric finite tensor categories over fields of positive characteristic. We prove the conjecture in the case of semisimple categories and more generally in the case of categories with fiber functors to the characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \gt 0$</tex> Verlinde category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SL_{2}$</tex>. We also construct a symmetric finite tensor category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm sVec}_{2}$</tex> over fields of characteristic 2 and show that it is a candidate for the category of supervector spaces in this characteristic. We further show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm sVec}_{2}$</tex> does not fiber over the characteristic 2 Verlinde category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SL_{2}$</tex> and then prove the conjecture for any category fibered over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm sVec}_{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Torsion Classes and t-Structures in Higher Homological Algebra
abstract: Higher homological algebra was introduced by Iyama. It is also known as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-homological algebra where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \geqslant 2$</tex> is a fixed integer, and it deals with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-cluster tilting subcategories of abelian categories. All short exact sequences in such a subcategory are split, but it has nice exact sequences with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n+2$</tex> objects. This was recently formalized by Jasso in the theory of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-abelian categories. There is also a derived version of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-homological algebra, formalized by Geiss, Keller, and Oppermann in the theory of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n+2)$</tex>-angulated categories (the reason for the shift from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n+2$</tex> is that angulated categories have triangulated categories as the “base case”). We introduce torsion classes and t-structures into the theory of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-abelian and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n+2)$</tex>-angulated categories, and prove several results to motivate the definitions. Most of the results concern the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-abelian and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n+2)$</tex>-angulated categories <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr {M}(\Lambda )$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr {C}(\Lambda )$</tex> associated to an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-representation finite algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda $</tex>, as defined by Iyama and Oppermann. We characterize torsion classes in these categories in terms of closure under higher extensions, and give a bijection between torsion classes in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr {M}(\Lambda )$</tex> and intermediate t-structures in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr {C}(\Lambda )$</tex> which is a category one can reasonably view as the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-derived category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr {M}(\Lambda )$</tex>. We hint at the link to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-homological tilting theory.

articleTitle: On Codazzi Tensors on a Hyperbolic Surface and Flat Lorentzian Geometry
abstract: Using global considerations, Mess proved that the moduli space of globally hyperbolic flat Lorentzian structures on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S\times {\BBR}$</tex> is the tangent bundle of the Teichmüller space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> is a closed surface. One of the goals of this paper is to deepen this surprising occurrence and to make explicit the relation between the Mess parameters and the embedding data of any Cauchy surface. This relation is pointed out by using some specific properties of Codazzi tensors on hyperbolic surfaces. As a by-product, we get a new Lorentzian proof of Goldman's celebrated result about the coincidence of the Weil–Petersson symplectic form and the Goldman pairing. In the second part of the paper, we use this machinery to get a classification of globally hyperbolic flat space-times with particles of angles in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0,2\pi )$</tex> containing a uniformly convex Cauchy surface. The analog of Mess' result is achieved showing that the corresponding moduli space is the tangent bundle of the Teichmüller space of a punctured surface. To generalize the theory in the case of particles, we deepen the study of Codazzi tensors on hyperbolic surfaces with cone singularities, proving that the well-known decomposition of a Codazzi tensor in a harmonic part and a trivial part can be generalized in the context of hyperbolic metrics with cone singularities.Communicated by Prof. Igor Rivin

articleTitle: Discontinuous Gradient Constraints and the Infinity Laplacian
abstract: Motivated by tug-of-war games and asymptotic analysis of certain variational problems, we consider the following gradient constraint problem: given a bounded domain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \subset {\BBR}^{n}$</tex>, a continuous function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\colon \partial \Omega \to {\BBR}$</tex>, and a nonempty subset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D\subset \Omega $</tex>, find a solution to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\cases {\min\{\Delta_\infty u, {\vert Du \vert}-\chi_D\}=0 {\$} \hbox{in } \Omega$\cr u=f {\$} \hbox{on } \partial\Omega,$}$$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta _\infty $</tex> is the infinity Laplace operator. We prove that this problem always has a solution that is unique if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {D} =\overline {{\rm int} D}$</tex>. If this regularity condition on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> fails, then solutions obtained from game theory and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^p$</tex>-approximation need not coincide.

articleTitle: Stability and Instability of the Einstein–Lichnerowicz Constraint System
abstract: We investigate the relevance of the conformal method by investigating stability issues for the Einstein–Lichnerowicz conformal constraint system in a nonlinear scalar-field setting. We prove the stability of the system with respect to arbitrary perturbations of generic focusing physics data on closed locally conformally flat manifolds, in any dimension. We also show that our stability result is sharp by constructing explicit instability examples when its assumptions are not satisfied. Our results apply to a more general class of constraint-like systems.

articleTitle: Quantum Dilogarithm Identities at Root of Unity
abstract: We study the root of unity degeneration of cluster algebras and quantum dilogarithm identities. We prove identities for the cyclic dilogarithm associated with a mutation sequence of a quiver, and as a consequence new identities for the noncompact quantum dilogarithm at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b=1$</tex>.Communicated by Michio Jimbo

articleTitle: The Jacquet–Langlands Correspondence via Twisted Descent
abstract: The existence of the well-known Jacquet–Langlands correspondence was established by Jacquet and Langlands via the trace formula method in 1970 [13]. An explicit construction of such a correspondence was obtained by Shimizu via theta series in 1972 [30]. In this paper, we extend the automorphic descent method of Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry [10] to a new setting. As a consequence, we recover the classical Jacquet–Langlands correspondence for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {PGL}}(2)$</tex> via a new explicit construction.

articleTitle: Integral Points of Fixed Degree and Bounded Height
abstract: By Northcott's Theorem there are only finitely many algebraic points in affine <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-space of fixed degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex> over a given number field and of height at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. Finding the asymptotics for these cardinalities as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> becomes large is a long-standing problem which is solved only for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e=1$</tex> by Schanuel, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=1$</tex> by Masser and Vaaler, and for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> “large enough” by Schmidt, Gao, and the author. In this paper, we study the case where the coordinates of the points are restricted to algebraic integers, and we derive the analogues of Schanuel's, Schmidt's, Gao's, and the author's results. The proof invokes tools from dynamics on homogeneous spaces, algebraic number theory, geometry of numbers, and a geometric partition method due to Schmidt.

articleTitle: Markov Traces on Affine and Cyclotomic Yokonuma–Hecke Algebras
abstract: In this article, we define and study the affine and cyclotomic Yokonuma–Hecke algebras. These algebras generalize at the same time the Ariki–Koike and affine Hecke algebras and the Yokonuma–Hecke algebras. We study the representation theory of these algebras and construct several bases for them. We then show how we can define Markov traces on them, which we in turn use to construct invariants for framed and classical knots in the solid torus. Finally, we study the Markov trace with zero parameters on the cyclotomic Yokonuma–Hecke algebras and determine the Schur elements with respect to that trace.

articleTitle: Multi-Way Expanders and Imprimitive Group Actions on Graphs
abstract: For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 2$</tex>, the concept of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-way expanders was defined by many researchers. Bigger <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> gives a weaker notion in general, and 2-way expanders coincide with expanders in usual sense. Koji Fujiwara asked whether these concepts are equivalent to that of ordinary expanders for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> for a sequence of Cayley graphs. In this paper, we answer his question in the affirmative. Furthermore, we obtain universal inequalities on multi-way isoperimetric constants on any finite connected vertex-transitive graph, and show that gaps between these constants imply the imprimitivity of the group action on the graph.

articleTitle: Equivariant Gromov–Witten Theory of Affine Smooth Toric Deligne–Mumford Stacks
abstract: For any finite abelian group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, the equivariant Gromov–Witten invariants of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[{\BBC}^r/G]$</tex> can be viewed as a certain kind of abelian Hurwitz–Hodge integrals. In this paper, we use Tseng's orbifold quantum Riemann–Roch theorem to express this kind of abelian Hurwitz–Hodge integrals as a sum over Feynman graphs, where the weight of each graph is expressed in terms of descendant integrals over moduli spaces of stable curves and representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>. This expression will play a crucial role in the proof of the remodeling conjecture for affine toric Calabi–Yau 3-orbifolds by the authors.

articleTitle: A Case of the Dynamical André–Oort Conjecture
abstract: We prove a special case of the Dynamical André–Oort Conjecture formulated by Baker and DeMarco [2]. For any integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\ge 2$</tex>, we show that for a rational plane curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> parameterized by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(t, h(t))$</tex> for some nonconstant polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h\in {\BBC}[z]$</tex>, if there exist infinitely many points <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(a,b)\in C({\BBC})$</tex> such that both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z^d+a$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z^d+b$</tex> are postcritically finite maps, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h(z)=\xi z$</tex> for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(d-1)$</tex>st root of unity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi $</tex>. As a key step in our proof, we show that the Mandelbrot set is not the filled Julia set of any polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\in {\BBC}[z]$</tex>.Communicated by Prof. Umberto Zannier

articleTitle: The Distribution of Gaps for Saddle Connections on the Octagon
abstract: We explicitly compute the limiting gap distribution for slopes of saddle connections on the flat surface associated to the regular octagon with opposite sides identified. This is the first such computation where the Veech group of the translation surface has multiple cusps. We also show how to parameterize a Poincaré section for the horocycle flow on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SL}(2,{\BBR})/{\rm SL}(X,\omega )$</tex> associated to an arbitrary Veech surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X, \omega )$</tex>. As a corollary, we show that the associated gap distribution is piecewise real analytic.

articleTitle: Mixed Tate Motives and the Unit Equation
abstract: This is the second installment in a sequence of articles devoted to “explicit Chabauty–Kim theory” for the thrice punctured line. Its ultimate goal is to construct an algorithmic solution to the unit equation whose halting will be conditional on Goncharov's conjecture about exhaustion of mixed Tate motives by motivic iterated integrals (refined somewhat with respect to ramification), and on Kim's conjecture about the determination of integral points via <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic iterated integrals. In this installment, we explain what this means while developing basic tools for the construction of the algorithm. We also work out an elaborate example, which goes beyond the cases that were understood before, and allows us to verify Kim's conjecture in a range of new cases.

articleTitle: Dominating Surface Group Representations by Fuchsian Ones
abstract: We prove that a representation from the fundamental group of a closed surface of negative Euler characteristic with values in the isometry group of a Riemannian manifold of sectional curvature bounded by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>1 can be dominated by a Fuchsian representation. Moreover, we prove that the domination can be made strict, unless the representation is discrete and faithful in restriction to an invariant totally geodesic 2-plane of curvature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>1. When applied to representations into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {PSL}(2,\mathbb {R})$</tex> of non-extremal Euler class, our result is a step forward in understanding the space of closed anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds.

articleTitle: Symmetric Webs, Jones–Wenzl Recursions, and q-Howe Duality
abstract: We define and study the category of symmetric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {sl}_{2}$</tex>-webs. This is a combinatorial description of the category of all finite-dimensional quantum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {sl}_{2}$</tex>-modules. Explicitly, we show that (the additive closure of) the category of symmetric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {sl}_{2}$</tex>-webs is (braided monoidally) equivalent to the latter. Our main tool is a quantum version of symmetric Howe duality. As a corollary of our construction, we provide new insight into Jones–Wenzl projectors and colored Jones polynomials.

articleTitle: Compositional (km, kn)-Shuffle Conjectures
abstract: In 2008, Haglund et al. [21] formulated a Compositional form of the Shuffle Conjecture of Haglund et al. [20]. In very recent work, Gorsky and Negut, by combining their discoveries [19, 25, 26] with the work of Schiffmann and Vasserot [28, 29] on the symmetric function side and the work of Hikita [22] and Gorsky and Mazin [18] on the combinatorial side, were led to formulate an infinite family of conjectures that extend the original Shuffle Conjecture of [20]. In fact, they formulated one conjecture for each pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(m,n)$</tex> of coprime integers. This work of Gorsky–Negut leads naturally to the question as to where the Compositional Shuffle Conjecture of Haglund–Morse–Zabrocki fits into these recent developments. Our contribution here is a compositional extension of the Gorsky–Negut Shuffle Conjecture for each pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(km,kn)$</tex>, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(m,n)$</tex> coprime and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \gt 1$</tex>.

articleTitle: Decomposition Matrices are Generically Trivial
abstract: We establish a genericity property in the representation theory of a flat family of finite-dimensional algebras in the sense of Cline–Parshal–Scott. More precisely, we show that the decomposition matrices as introduced by Geck and Rouquier of an algebra that is free of finite dimension over a noetherian integral domain and that splits over the fraction field of this ring are generically trivial, that is, they are trivial in an open neighborhood of the generic point of the spectrum of the base ring. This generalizes a classical result by Brauer in modular representation theory of finite groups. We furthermore show that this is true precisely on an open set in case all fibers of the algebra split. In this way, we get a stratification of the base scheme such that decomposition maps are trivial on each stratum. Moreover, this defines a new discriminant of such algebras which generalizes Schur elements of simple modules for symmetric split semisimple algebras. We provide some extensions to the theory of decomposition maps allowing us to work without the usual normality assumption on the base ring.

articleTitle: On Deficiency Gradient of Groups
abstract: Deficiency gradient is a higher dimensional analog of rank gradient. In this paper, we give a combinatorial proof that the fundamental group of a simply connected complex of amenable groups has deficiency gradient zero. We apply this to establish the vanishing of deficiency gradient in special linear groups over polynomial rings and number fields, and in Artin groups for which the nerve of the Coxeter matrix is simply connected. This implies that the first and second <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l^2$</tex>-Betti numbers vanish for these Artin groups without recourse to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K(\pi ,1)$</tex> conjecture. We propose a conjecture about the stabilization of deficiency gradient, which characterizes groups with 2-dimensional classifying spaces.Communicated by Marc Burger

articleTitle: Degree 3 Cohomology of Function Fields of Surfaces
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> be the function field of a surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> over a finite field. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l$</tex> be a prime not equal to the characteristic of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>. Our main result is a local–global principle (with respect to discrete valuations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>) for a class in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^3(F, \mu _l^{\otimes 3})$</tex> to be written as the cup product of a given symbol in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^2(F, \mu _l^{\otimes 2})$</tex> by some class in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^1(F, \mu _l) \simeq F^*/F^{*l}$</tex>. From this, we deduce if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> contains a primitive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l{\rm th}$</tex> root of unity, then any element in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^3(F, \mu _l^{\otimes 3})$</tex> is represented by a symbol, a result which was previously known only for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l = 2$</tex>. The local–global principle also enables us to show that if a three-fold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> over a finite field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBF}$</tex> (with char<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\BBF}) \neq 2$</tex>) admits a conic bundle fibration over a surface, then the unramified cohomology group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^3_{nr}({\BBF}(X)/{\BBF}, {\BBZ}/2)$</tex> vanishes. Combined with earlier works, this gives a proof of the integral Tate conjecture for one-cycles on certain classes of three-fold over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBF}$</tex>. It also leads to a proof that the Brauer–Manin obstruction to existence of a zero-cycle of degree 1 is the only obstruction for a certain classes of surfaces over global fields of positive characteristic.

articleTitle: New Simple Lie Algebras in Characteristic 2
abstract: Several improvements of the Kostrikin–Shafarevich method conjecturally producing all simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras over algebraically closed fields of any positive characteristic were recently suggested; the list of examples obtained by the improved method becomes richer but in characteristic 2 it is far from being saturated. We investigate one of the steps of our version of the method; in characteristic 2 we describe several new simple Lie algebras and interpret several other simple Lie algebras, previously known only as sums of their components, as Lie algebras of vector fields.Several new simple Lie superalgebras can be constructed from the newly found simple Lie algebras. We also describe one new simple Lie superalgebra in characteristic 3; it is the only simple Lie superalgebra missed in the approach taken in [6].

articleTitle: Poincaré Duality of Wonderful Compactifications and Tautological Rings
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g \geq 2$</tex>. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {M}_{g,n}^{rt}$</tex> be the moduli space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-pointed genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> curves with rational tails. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {C}_g^n$</tex> be the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-fold fibered power of the universal curve over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {M}_g$</tex>. We prove that the tautological ring of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {M}_{g,n}^{rt}$</tex> has Poincaré duality if and only if the same holds for the tautological ring of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {C}_g^n$</tex>. We also obtain a presentation of the tautological ring of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {M}_{g,n}^{rt}$</tex> as an algebra over the tautological ring of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {C}_g^n$</tex>. This proves a conjecture of Tavakol. Our results are valid in the more general setting of wonderful compactifications.

articleTitle: Poisson Geometry of Monic Matrix Polynomials
abstract: We study the Poisson geometry of the first congruence subgroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_1[z^{-1}]$</tex> of the loop group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G[z^{-1}]$</tex> endowed with the rational r-matrix Poisson structure for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G={\rm GL}_m$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SL}_m$</tex>. We classify all the symplectic leaves on a certain ind-subvariety of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_1[z^{-1}]$</tex> in terms of Smith Normal Forms. This classification extends known descriptions of symplectic leaves on the (thin) affine Grassmannian and the space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SL}_m$</tex>-monopoles. We show that a generic leaf is covered by open charts with Poisson transition functions, the charts being birationally isomorphic to products of coadjoint <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}_m$</tex> orbits. Finally, we discuss our results in terms of (thick) affine Grassmannians and Zastava spaces.

articleTitle: The Distribution of 𝔽q-Points on Cyclic ℓ-Covers of Genus g
abstract: We study fluctuations in the number of points of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-cyclic covers of the projective line over the finite field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBF}_q$</tex> when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q \equiv 1\hbox { mod}\,\ell $</tex> is fixed and the genus tends to infinity. The distribution is given as a sum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q+1$</tex> i.i.d. random variables. This was settled for hyperelliptic curves by Kurlberg and Rudnick [7], while statistics were obtained for certain components of the moduli space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-cyclic covers in [1]. In this paper, we obtain statistics for the distribution of the number of points as the covers vary over the full moduli space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-cyclic covers of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>. This is achieved by relating <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-covers to cyclic function field extensions, and counting such extensions with prescribed ramification and splitting conditions at a finite number of primes.

articleTitle: On the Number of p'-Degree Characters in a Finite Group
abstract: Let p be a prime divisor of the order of a finite group G. Then G has at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \sqrt {p-1}$</tex> complex irreducible characters of degrees prime to p. In case p is a prime with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt {p-1}$</tex> an integer this bound is sharp for infinitely many groups G.

articleTitle: On Complex Highly Regular Embeddings and the Extended Vassiliev Conjecture
abstract: A continuous map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {C}^d\longrightarrow \mathbb {C}^N$</tex> is a complex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-regular embedding if any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> pairwise distinct points in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {C}^d$</tex> are mapped by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> complex linearly independent vectors in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {C}^N$</tex>. The existence of such maps is closely connected with classical problems of algebraic/differential topology, such as embedding/immersion problems. Our central result on complex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-regular embeddings extends results of Cohen & Handel (1978), Chisholm (1979) and Blagojević, Lück & Ziegler (2013) on real <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-regular embeddings. We give the following lower bounds for the existence of complex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-regular embeddings. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> be an odd prime, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k\geq 1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=p^t$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t\geq 1$</tex>. If there exists a complex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-regular embedding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {C}^d\longrightarrow \mathbb {C}^N$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ d(k-\alpha _p(k))+\alpha _p(k)\leq N$</tex>. Here <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha _p(k)$</tex> denotes the sum of coefficients in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic expansion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>. These lower bounds are obtained by modifying the framework of Cohen & Handel (1978) and a study of Chern classes of complex regular representations. As a main technical result we establish for this an extended Vassiliev conjecture, the following upper bound for the height of the cohomology of an unordered configuration space: If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq 2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k\geq 2$</tex> are integers, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> is an odd prime. Then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\mathfrak{h}\left(H^*\left(F\left(\mathbb{R}^d,k\right)/\mathfrak{S}_k;\mathbb{F}_p\right)\right)\leq\min\left\{p^t: 2p^t\geq d \right\}.$$</tex> Furthermore, we give similar lower bounds for the existence of complex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-skew embeddings <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {C}^d\longrightarrow \mathbb {C}^N$</tex>, for which we require that the images of the tangent spaces at any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex> distinct points are skew complex affine subspaces of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {C}^N$</tex>. In addition we give improved lower bounds for the Lusternik–Schnirelmann category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F(\mathbb {C}^d,k)/\mathfrak {S}_k$</tex> as well as for the sectional category of the covering <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F(\mathbb {C}^d,k)\longrightarrow F(\mathbb {C}^d,k)/\mathfrak {S}_k$</tex>.

articleTitle: Birational Geometry of the Moduli Space of Rank 2 Parabolic Vector Bundles on a Rational Curve
abstract: We investigate the birational geometry (in the sense of Mori's program) of the moduli space of rank 2 semistable parabolic vector bundles on a rational curve. We compute the effective cone of the moduli space and show that all birational models obtained by Mori's program are also moduli spaces of parabolic vector bundles with certain parabolic weights.

articleTitle: M-Systems and Cluster Algebras
abstract: The aim of this paper is two-fold: (1) to introduce four systems of equations called M-systems and dual M-systems of types <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{n}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{n}$</tex>, respectively; (2) to make a connection between M-systems (dual M-systems) and cluster algebras, and prove that the Hernandez–Leclerc conjecture is true for minimal affinizations of types <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_n$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_n$</tex>.

articleTitle: On the Exotic t-Structure in Positive Characteristic
abstract: In this paper, we study Bezrukavnikov's exotic t-structure on the derived category of equivariant coherent sheaves on the Springer resolution of a connected reductive algebraic group defined over a field of positive characteristic with simply connected derived subgroup. In particular, we show that the heart of the exotic t-structure is a graded highest weight category, and we study the tilting objects in this heart. Our main tool is the “geometric braid group action” studied by Bezrukavnikov and the second author.

articleTitle: Non-commutative Desingularization of Determinantal Varieties, II: Arbitrary Minors
abstract: In our paper “Non-commutative desingularization of determinantal varieties I”, we constructed and studied non-commutative resolutions of determinantal varieties defined by maximal minors. At the end of the introduction, we asserted that the results could be generalized to determinantal varieties defined by non-maximal minors, at least in characteristic zero. In this paper, we prove the existence of non-commutative resolutions in the general case in a manner which is still characteristic free, and carry out the explicit description by generators and relations in characteristic zero. As an application of our results, we prove that there is a fully faithful embedding between the bounded derived categories of the two canonical (commutative) resolutions of a determinantal variety, confirming a well-known conjecture of Bondal and Orlov in this special case.

articleTitle: Locally Conformally Symplectic Structures on Compact Non-Kähler Complex Surfaces
abstract: We prove that every compact complex surface with odd first Betti number admits a locally conformally symplectic 2-form which tames the underlying almost complex structure.

articleTitle: Spherical Sets Avoiding a Prescribed Set of Angles
abstract: Let Xbe any subset of the interval [−1, 1]. A subset Iof the unit sphere in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^n$</tex> will be called X-avoiding if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<u,v>\not\in X$</tex> for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u,v\in I$</tex>. The problem of determining the maximum surface measure of a {0}-avoiding set was first stated in a 1974 note by Witsenhausen; there the upper bound of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/n$</tex> times the surface measure of the sphere is derived from a simple averaging argument. A consequence of the Frankl–Wilson theorem is that this fraction decreases exponentially, but until now the 1/3 upper bound for the case n= 3 has not moved. We improve this bound to 0.313 using an approach inspired by Delsarte's linear programming bounds for codes, combined with some combinatorial reasoning. In the second part of the paper, we use harmonic analysis to show that, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq3$</tex>, there always exists an X-avoiding set of maximum measure. We also show with an example that a maximizer need not exist when n= 2.

articleTitle: Phase Stability for Schrödinger–Poisson Critical Systems in Closed 5-Manifolds
abstract: We conclude in this article the investigation of the stability properties of the Schrödinger–Poisson critical system <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{cases} \Delta_g u+ \omega^2 u +\varphi u = u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}},\\ \Delta_g \varphi +m_0^2 \varphi = 4\pi q^2 u^2, \end{cases}\qquad(0.1)$$</tex> on a closed Riemannian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-manifold, initiated in Hebey–Wei [15] and pursued in Thizy [22–25]. We prove that all phases in the system are stable in dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=5$</tex>, and that this phase stability holds true without any kind of geometric assumptions on the manifold. Owing to the blow-up examples in Thizy [22], where sequences of solutions with unbounded energy are constructed in specific five-dimensional manifolds, we then get a complete description of the blow-up phenomena for the Schrödinger–Poisson critical system in this dimension.

articleTitle: CB-Norm Estimates for Maps Between Noncommutative Lp-Spaces and Quantum Channel Theory
abstract: In the first part of this work, we show how certain techniques from quantum information theory can be used in order to obtain very sharp embeddings between noncommutative <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{p}$</tex>-spaces. Then, we use these estimates to study the classical capacity with restricted assisted entanglement of the quantum erasure channel and the quantum depolarizing channel. In particular, we exactly compute the capacity of the first one and we show that certain nonmultiplicative results hold for the second one.

articleTitle: Geometric Convergence of the Kähler–Ricci Flow on Complex Surfaces of General Type
abstract: We show that on smooth minimal surfaces of general type, the Kähler–Ricci flow starting at any initial Kähler metric converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a Kähler–Einstein orbifold surface. In particular, the diameter of the evolving metrics is uniformly bounded for all time, and the Kähler–Ricci flow contracts all the holomorphic spheres with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-2)$</tex> self-intersection number to isolated orbifold points. Our estimates do not require a priori the existence of an orbifold Kähler–Einstein metric on the canonical model.

articleTitle: The Splitting Process in Free Probability Theory
abstract: Free cumulants were introduced by Speicher as a proper analog of classical cumulants in Voiculescu's theory of free probability. The relation between free moments and free cumulants is usually described in terms of Möbius calculus over the lattice of non-crossing partitions. In this work, we explore another approach to free cumulants and to their combinatorial study using a combinatorial Hopf algebra structure on the linear span of non-crossing partitions. The generating series of free moments is seen as a character on this Hopf algebra. It is characterized by solving a linear fixed-point equation that relates it to the generating series of free cumulants. These phenomena are explained through a process similar to (though different from) the arborification process familiar in the theory of dynamical systems, and originating in Cayley's work.

articleTitle: Perturbations of Weyl Sums
Large Deviations for Rough Path Lifts of Watanabe's Pullbacks of Delta Functions
abstract: We study Donsker–Watanabe's delta functions associated with strongly hypoelliptic diffusion processes indexed by a small parameter. They are finite Borel measures on the Wiener space and admit a rough path lift. Our main result is a large deviation principle (LDP) of Schilder type for the lifted measures on the geometric rough path space as the scale parameter tends to zero. As a corollary, we obtain an LDP conjectured by Takanobu and Watanabe, which is a generalization of an LDP of Freidlin–Wentzell type for pinned diffusion processes.

articleTitle: Homomorphisms Between Scalar Generalized Verma Modules for gl(n, ℂ)
abstract: In this article, we classify the homomorphisms between scalar generalized Verma modules for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\Fraktur g}{\Fraktur l}(n,{\BBC})$</tex>. In fact such homomorphisms are compositions of elementary homomorphisms.

articleTitle: A Bott-Type Residue Formula on Complex Orbifolds
abstract: We prove residual formulas for vector fields defined on compact complex orbifolds with isolated singularities and give some applications of these on weighted projective spaces.

articleTitle: One-Dimensional Interpolation Inequalities, Carlson–Landau Inequalities, and Magnetic Schrödinger Operators
abstract: In this paper, we prove refined first-order interpolation inequalities for periodic functions and give applications to various refinements of the Carlson–Landau-type inequalities and to magnetic Schrödinger operators. We also obtain Lieb–Thirring inequalities for magnetic Schrödinger operators on multi-dimensional cylinders.

articleTitle: Combinatorial Frameworks for Cluster Algebras
abstract: We develop a general approach to finding combinatorial models for cluster algebras. The approach is to construct a labeled graph called a framework. When a framework is constructed with certain properties, the result is a model incorporating information about exchange matrices, principal coefficients, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf g}$</tex>-vectors, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf g}$</tex>-vector fans. The idea behind frameworks arises from Cambrian combinatorics and sortable elements, and in this paper, we use sortable elements to construct a framework for any cluster algebra with an acyclic initial exchange matrix. This Cambrian framework yields a model of the entire exchange graph when the cluster algebra is of finite type. Outside of finite type, the Cambrian framework models only part of the exchange graph. In a forthcoming paper, we extend the Cambrian construction to produce a complete framework for a cluster algebra whose associated Cartan matrix is of affine type.

articleTitle: Ricci Flow Emerging from Rotationally Symmetric Degenerate Neckpinches
abstract: In [3], the authors created Type-II Ricci flow neckpinch singularities. In this paper, we construct solutions to Ricci flow whose initial data are the singular metric resulting from these singularities. We show in particular that the curvature decreases at the same rate at which it blew up. This is the first example of Ricci flow starting from a Type-II singularity.

articleTitle: Functional Versions of Lp-Affine Surface Area and Entropy Inequalities
abstract: In contemporary convex geometry, the rapidly developing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex>-Brunn–Minkowski theory is a modern analog of the classical Brunn–Minkowski theory. A central notion of this theory is the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex>-affine surface area of convex bodies. Here, we introduce a functional analog of this concept, for log-concave and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>-concave functions. We show that the new analytic notion is a generalization of the original <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex>-affine surface area. We prove duality relations and affine isoperimetric inequalities for log-concave and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>-concave functions. This leads to a new inverse log-Sobolev inequality for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>-concave densities.

articleTitle: Commuting Ordinary Differential Operators with Polynomial Coefficients and Automorphisms of the First Weyl Algebra
abstract: In this paper, we study rank 2 commuting ordinary differential operators with polynomial coefficients and the orbit space of the automorphisms group of the first Weyl algebra on such operators. We prove that for arbitrary fixed spectral curve of genus one the space of orbits is infinite. Moreover, we prove in this case that for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\ge 1$</tex> there is a pair of self-adjoint commuting ordinary differential operators of rank 2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_4=(\partial _x^2+V(x))^2+W(x)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{6}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W(x),V(x)$</tex> are polynomials of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n+2$</tex>. We also prove that there are hyperelliptic spectral curves with the infinite spaces of orbits.

articleTitle: Spectra of Lens Spaces from 1-Norm Spectra of Congruence Lattices
abstract: To every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional lens space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>, we associate a congruence lattice <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal L$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ}^m$</tex>, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=2m-1$</tex> and we prove a formula relating the multiplicities of Hodge–Laplace eigenvalues on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> with the number of lattice elements of a given <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\|{\cdot }\|_1$</tex>-length in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal L$</tex>. As a consequence, we show that two lens spaces are isospectral on functions (respectively, isospectral on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-forms for every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>) if and only if the associated congruence lattices are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\|{\cdot }\|_1$</tex>-isospectral (respectively, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\|{\cdot }\|_1$</tex>-isospectral plus a geometric condition). Using this fact, we give, for every dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\ge 5$</tex>, infinitely many examples of Riemannian manifolds that are isospectral on every level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> and are not strongly isospectral.

articleTitle: Delaunay-Type Hypersurfaces in Cohomogeneity One Manifolds
abstract: Classical Delaunay surfaces are highly symmetric constant mean curvature (CMC) submanifolds of space forms. We prove the existence of Delaunay-type hypersurfaces in a large class of compact manifolds, using the geometry of cohomogeneity one group actions and variational bifurcation techniques. Our construction specializes to the classical examples in round spheres, and allows to obtain Delaunay-type hypersurfaces in many other ambient spaces, ranging from complex and quaternionic projective spaces to Kervaire exotic spheres.

articleTitle: Integrable Systems from the Classical Reflection Equation
abstract: We construct integrable Hamiltonian systems on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G/K$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is a coboundary Poisson–Lie group and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is a Lie subgroup arising as the fixed point set of a group automorphism <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma $</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> satisfying the classical reflection equation. We show that the time evolution of these systems is described by a Lax equation, and under a factorizability assumption, present its solution in terms of a factorization problem in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>. Our construction is closely related to the semiclassical limit of Sklyanin's integrable quantum spin chains with reflecting boundaries.Communicated by Anton Alekseev

articleTitle: On the Fundamental Group Scheme of Rationally Chain-Connected Varieties
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> be an algebraically closed field. Chambert-Loir proved that the étale fundamental group of a proper normal rationally chain-connected variety over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> is finite.
