We prove that the fundamental group scheme of a proper normal rationally chain-connected variety over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> is finite too. In particular, the fundamental group scheme of a Fano variety is finite.

articleTitle: Order Structure and Topological Properties of the Set of Multiple Zeta Values
abstract: In this paper, we classify all the convergent sequences of multiple zeta values which do not converge to 0. Using this classification, we completely describe the iterated derived sets of the set of multiple zeta values in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}$</tex>. Our results imply that the set of multiple zeta values, ordered by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq $</tex>, is a well-ordered set. We determine its type of order, which is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega ^3$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega $</tex> is the smallest infinite ordinal.

articleTitle: Cells and Cacti
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(W,S)$</tex> be a Coxeter system, let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi $</tex> be a weight function on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S,$</tex> and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\rm Cact}}_W$</tex> denote the associated cactus group. Following an idea of I. Losev, we construct an action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\rm Cact}}_W \times {{\rm Cact}}_W$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> that has nice properties with respect to the partition of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> into left, right, or two-sided cells (under some hypothesis, which hold for instance if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi $</tex> is constant). It must be noted that the action depends heavily on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi $</tex>.

articleTitle: Bilinear Forms with GL3 Kloosterman Sums and the Spectral Large Sieve
abstract: We analyze certain bilinear forms involving <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_3$</tex> Kloosterman sums. As an application, we obtain an improved estimate for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_3$</tex> spectral large sieve inequality.

articleTitle: Bezout Inequality for Mixed Volumes
abstract: In this article, we consider the following analog of Bezout inequality for mixed volumes: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$V(P_1,\dots,P_r,\Delta^{n-r})V_n{(\Delta)}^{r-1}\leq\prod_{i=1}^rV(P_i,\Delta^{n-1})\text{ for }2\leq r\leq n.$$</tex> We show that the above inequality is true when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex> is an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional simplex and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_1,\dots,P_r$</tex> are convex bodies in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^n$</tex>. We conjecture that if the above inequality is true for all convex bodies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_1,\dots,P_r$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex> must be an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional simplex. We prove that if the above inequality is true for all convex bodies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_1,\dots,P_r$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex> must be indecomposable (i.e., cannot be written as the Minkowski sum of two convex bodies which are not homothetic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex>), which confirms the conjecture when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex> is a simple polytope and in the two-dimensional case. Finally, we connect the inequality to an inequality on the volume of orthogonal projections of convex bodies as well as prove an isomorphic version of the inequality.

articleTitle: Boundary-Reducing and Toroidal Dehn Fillings at the Maximal Distance
abstract: If a hyperbolic 3-manifold admits boundary-reducing and toroidal Dehn fillings on a torus boundary component, then the distance between the filling slopes is known to be at most 2. In this paper, we determine all hyperbolic 3-manifolds admitting such a pair of Dehn fillings at distance 2.

articleTitle: Finite Functorial Semi-Norms and Representability
abstract: Functorial semi-norms are semi-normed refinements of functors such as singular (co)homology. We investigate how different types of representability affect the (non-)triviality of finite functorial semi-norms on certain functors or classes. In particular, we consider representable functors, generalized cohomology theories, and so-called weakly flexible homology classes in singular homology and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell ^1$</tex>-homology.

articleTitle: Dynamic Alpha-invariants of Del Pezzo Surfaces
abstract: For every smooth del Pezzo surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>, smooth curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C\in |-K_{S}|$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta \in (0,1]$</tex>, we compute the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex>-invariant of Tian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha (S,(1-\beta )C)$</tex> and prove the existence of Kähler–Einstein metrics on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> with edge singularities along <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> of angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\pi \beta $</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta $</tex> in certain interval. In particular, we give lower bounds for the invariant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R(S,C)$</tex>, introduced by Donaldson as the supremum of all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta \in (0,1]$</tex> for which such a metric exists. The pairs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S,C)$</tex> considered are strongly asymptotically log del Pezzo surfaces. We study one of the two classes of such pairs for which such metrics are expected to exist for all small <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta \gt 0$</tex>.

articleTitle: RTT Realization of Quantum Affine Superalgebras and Tensor Products
abstract: We use the RTT realization of the quantum affine superalgebra associated with the Lie superalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {gl}(M,N)$</tex> to study its finite-dimensional representations and their tensor products. In the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {gl}(1,1)$</tex>, the cyclicity condition of tensor products of finite-dimensional simple modules is determined completely in terms of zeros and poles of rational functions. This in turn induces cyclicity of some particular tensor products of Kirillov–Reshetikhin modules related to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {gl}(M,N)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Linear Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
abstract: In [7], we introduced Laurent phenomenon algebras, a generalization of cluster algebras. Here we give an explicit description of Laurent phenomenon algebras with a linear initial seed arising from a graph. In particular, any graph associahedron is shown to be the dual cluster complex for some Laurent phenomenon algebra.

articleTitle: Gepner Type Stability Condition via Orlov/Kuznetsov Equivalence
abstract: We show the existence of Gepner-type Bridgeland stability conditions on triangulated categories of graded matrix factorizations associated to homogenous polynomials which define general cubic four-fold containing a plane. The key ingredient is to describe the grade shift functor of matrix factorizations in terms of sheaves of Clifford algebras on the projective plane under Orlov/Kuznetsov equivalence.

articleTitle: Polish Groups with Metrizable Universal Minimal Flows
abstract: We prove that if the universal minimal flow of a Polish group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is metrizable and contains a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_\delta $</tex> orbit <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G \cdot x_0$</tex>, then it is isomorphic to the completion of the homogeneous space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G/G_{x_0}$</tex> and show how this result translates naturally in terms of structural Ramsey theory. We also investigate universal minimal proximal flows and describe concrete representations of them in a number of examples.

articleTitle: Random Extensions of Free Groups and Surface Groups are Hyperbolic
abstract: In this note, we prove that a random extension of either the free group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_N$</tex> of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N\ge 3$</tex> or of the fundamental group of a closed, orientable surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_g$</tex> of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\ge 2$</tex> is a hyperbolic group. Here, a random extension is one corresponding to a subgroup of either <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Out}(F_N)$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Mod}(S_g)$</tex> generated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> independent random walks. Our main theorem is that a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-generated random subgroup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Mod}(S_g)$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Out}(F_N)$</tex> is free of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> and convex cocompact. More generally, we show that a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-generated random subgroup of a weakly hyperbolic group is free and undistorted.Communicated by Prof. Igor Rivin

articleTitle: A Geometric Study of Wasserstein Spaces: Isometric Rigidity in Negative Curvature
abstract: Given a metric space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>, one defines its Wasserstein space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\scr {W}_2}(X)$</tex> as a set of sufficiently decaying probability measures on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> endowed with a metric defined from optimal transportation. In this article, we continue the geometric study of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\scr {W}_2}(X)$</tex> when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is a simply connected, non-positively curved metric spaces by considering its isometry group. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is Euclidean, the second-named author proved that this isometry group is larger than the isometry group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. In contrast, we prove here a rigidity result: when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is negatively curved, any isometry of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\scr {W}_2}(X)$</tex> comes from an isometry of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Chromatic Number of Random Graphs for Most Average Degrees
abstract: For a fixed number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d \gt 0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> large, let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(n,d/n)$</tex> be the random graph on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> vertices in which any two vertices are connected with probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d/n$</tex> independently. The problem of determining the chromatic number of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(n,d/n)$</tex> goes back to the famous 1960 article of Erdös and Rényi that started the theory of random graphs [Magayar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutato Int. Kozl. 5 (1960) 17–61]. Progress culminated in the landmark paper of Achlioptas and Naor [Ann. Math. 162 (2005) 1333–1349], in which they calculate the chromatic number precisely for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> in a set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S\subset (0,\infty )$</tex> of asymptotic density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lim _{z\rightarrow \infty } {1 \over z}\int _0^z{\bf 1}_S={1 \over 2}$</tex>, and up to an additive error of one for the remaining <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>. Here we obtain a near-complete answer by determining the chromatic number of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(n,d/n)$</tex> for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> in a set of asymptotic density 1.

articleTitle: Fock Spaces and Refined Severi Degrees
abstract: In this note we show that, for a large class of pairs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S,L)$</tex> of a toric surface with an ample line bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>, containing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^2$</tex> and rational-ruled surfaces, the refined Severi degrees can be computed as matrix elements of an operator on a Fock space. The Heisenberg algebra does not depend on the surface considered, only the operator. The result also applies to the Severi degrees counting complex curves and the Welschinger numbers which are a signed count of real curves.

articleTitle: Shimura Curves within the Locus of Hyperelliptic Jacobians in Genus 3
abstract: We construct an infinite number of Shimura curves contained in the locus of hyperelliptic Jacobians of genus 3. In the opposite direction, we show that in genus 3 the only possible non-complete (in the moduli space of abelian three-folds) Kuga curves contained in the hyperelliptic locus have the same degeneration data as that of the examples we construct. The locus of genus 3 hyperelliptic Jacobians is a divisor within the moduli space of principally polarized abelian three-folds, and our result demonstrates the techniques we develop more generally for dealing with Shimura curves contained within a divisor in the moduli space of abelian varieties.

articleTitle: The Moduli Scheme of Affine Spherical Varieties with a Free Weight Monoid
abstract: We study Alexeev and Brion's moduli scheme <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm M}_{\Gamma }$</tex> of affine spherical varieties with weight monoid <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> under the assumption that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> is free. We describe the tangent space to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm M}_{\Gamma }$</tex> at its “most degenerate point” in terms of the combinatorial invariants of spherical varieties and deduce that the irreducible components of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm M}_{\Gamma }$</tex>, equipped with their reduced induced scheme structure, are affine spaces.

articleTitle: Bounds on the Speed of Type II Blow-up for the Energy Critical Wave Equation in the Radial Case
abstract: We consider the focusing energy-critical wave equation in space dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N \in \{3, 4, 5\}$</tex> for radial data. We study type II blow-up solutions which concentrate one bubble of energy. It is known that such solutions decompose in the energy space as a sum of the bubble and an asymptotic profile. We prove bounds on the blow-up speed in the case when the asymptotic profile is sufficiently regular. These bounds are optimal in dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N = 5$</tex>. We also prove that if the asymptotic profile is sufficiently regular, then it cannot be strictly negative at the origin.

articleTitle: Primeness Results for von Neumann Algebras Associated with Surface Braid Groups
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of non-amenable groups denoted by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf NC}_1 \cap {\bf Quot}(\cal C_{rss})$</tex> which give rise to prime von Neumann algebras. This means that, for every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \in {\bf NC}_1 \cap {\bf Quot}(\cal {C}_{rss}),$</tex> its group von Neumann algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(\Gamma )$</tex> cannot be decomposed as a tensor product of diffuse von Neumann algebras. We show <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf NC}_1 \cap {\bf Quot}(\cal C_{rss})$</tex> is fairly large as it contains many examples of groups intensively studied in various areas of mathematics, notably: all infinite central quotients of pure surface braid groups; all mapping class groups of (punctured) surfaces of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0,1,2$</tex>; most Torelli groups and Johnson kernels of (punctured) surfaces of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0,1,2$</tex>; and all groups hyperbolic relative to finite families of residually finite, exact, infinite, proper subgroups.

articleTitle: Smooth Billiards with a Large Weyl Remainder
abstract: We prove an estimate from below for the remainder in Weyl's law for smooth star-shaped planar domains admitting an appropriate one-parameter family of periodic billiard trajectories. Examples include ellipses and smooth domains of constant width. Our results confirm a prediction of P. Sarnak who proved a similar statement for surfaces without boundary. The proof is based on the analysis of the singularity in the wave trace, occurring at time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T \gt 0$</tex> equal to the length of the closed trajectories belonging to the family. Such families of periodic orbits produce large singularities in the wave trace, which in turn imply estimates from below for the absolute value of the Weyl remainder averaged over a spectral window. We also obtain lower bounds for the error term in higher dimensions. In this case, the main contribution to the Weyl remainder typically comes from the singularity at zero of the wave trace. However, for certain domains, such as the Euclidean ball, the dimension of the family of periodic trajectories is large enough to dominate the contribution of the singularity at zero.

articleTitle: Silting Modules
abstract: We introduce the new concept of silting modules. These modules generalize tilting modules over an arbitrary ring, as well as support <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau $</tex>-tilting modules over a finite dimensional algebra recently introduced by Adachi, Iyama, and Reiten. We show that silting modules generate torsion classes that provide left approximations, and that every partial silting module admits an analog of the Bongartz complement. Furthermore, we prove that silting modules are in bijection with 2-term silting complexes and with certain t-structures and co-t-structures in the derived module category. We also see how some of these bijections hold for silting complexes of arbitrary finite length.

articleTitle: Local Gauge Conditions for Ellipticity in Conformal Geometry
abstract: In this article, we introduce local gauge conditions under which many curvature tensors appearing in conformal geometry, such as the Weyl, Cotton, Bach, and Fefferman–Graham obstruction tensors, become elliptic operators. The gauge conditions amount to fixing an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-harmonic coordinate system and normalizing the determinant of the metric. We also give corresponding elliptic regularity results and characterizations of local conformal flatness in low regularity settings.

articleTitle: Movable Curves and Semistable Sheaves
abstract: This paper extends a number of known results on slope-semistable sheaves from the classical case to the setting where polarizations are given by movable curve classes. As applications, we obtain new flatness results for reflexive sheaves on singular varieties, as well as a characterization of finite quotients of Abelian varieties via a Chern class condition.

articleTitle: Random Matrix Ensembles with Singularities and a Hierarchy of Painlevé III Equations
abstract: We study unitary invariant random matrix ensembles with singular potentials. We obtain asymptotics for the partition functions associated to the Laguerre and Gaussian Unitary Ensembles perturbed with a pole of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> at the origin, in the double scaling limit where the size of the matrices grows, and at the same time the strength of the pole decreases at an appropriate speed. In addition, we obtain double scaling asymptotics of the correlation kernel for a general class of ensembles of positive-definite Hermitian matrices perturbed with a pole. Our results are described in terms of a hierarchy of higher order analogs to the PIII equation, which reduces to the PIII equation itself when the pole is simple.

articleTitle: Formal Group Exponentials and Galois Modules in Lubin–Tate Extensions
abstract: The main result of this paper is the construction of overconvergent power series with coefficients in Lubin–Tate extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic fields. Using the values of these series at certain units we then construct integral Galois module generators in certain wildly ramified extensions and also obtain a new description of the Galois action in Lubin–Tate extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic fields. The motivation for this work came from recent progress with open questions on integral Galois module structure in wildly ramified extensions of number fields as a consequence of explicit descriptions of local integral Galois module generators in certain extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic fields due to Pickett. In parallel, Pulita has generalized the theory of Dwork's power series to a set of power series with coefficients in Lubin–Tate extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}_p$</tex>.In this paper, we generalize both Pulita's power series and Pickett's constructions using a combination of several tools: formal group exponentials, ramified Witt vectors and Lubin–Tate theory.

articleTitle: Quantum Ergodicity and Averaging Operators on the Sphere
abstract: We prove quantum ergodicity for certain orthonormal bases of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2({\BBS}^2)$</tex>, consisting of joint eigenfunctions of the Laplacian on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBS}^2$</tex> and the discrete averaging operator over a finite set of rotations, generating a free group. If, in addition, the rotations are algebraic, we give a quantified version of this result. The methods used also give a new, simplified proof of quantum ergodicity for large regular graphs.

articleTitle: Convergence of Kähler–Ricci Flow on Lower-Dimensional Algebraic Manifolds of General Type
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^4$</tex>-norm of Ricci curvature is uniformly bounded along a Kähler–Ricci flow on any minimal algebraic manifold. As an application, we show that on any minimal algebraic manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> of general type and with dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\le 3$</tex>, any solution of the normalized Kähler–Ricci flow converges to the unique singular Kähler–Einstein metric on the canonical model of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> in the Cheeger–Gromov topology.

articleTitle: Hyperpolygons and Hitchin Systems
abstract: We study the hyperkähler analogues of moduli spaces of semistable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-gons in complex projective space. We prove that the hyperkähler Kirwan map is surjective and produce a formula that recursively calculates the Betti numbers of these spaces for all ranks. Building on a natural analogy between hyperpolygons and parabolic Higgs bundles, we identify hyperpolygon spaces with certain degenerate Hitchin systems, and use this to establish their complete integrability, for ranks up to and including 3.

Estimates for Character Sums and Dirichlet L-Functions to Smooth Moduli
abstract: We use the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-analogue of van der Corput's method to estimate short character sums to smooth moduli. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi $</tex> is a primitive Dirichlet character modulo a squarefree, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q^\delta $</tex>-smooth integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex> we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$L\left({1 \over 2},\chi\right)\ll_\epsilon q^{{27 \over 164}+O\left(\delta\right)+\epsilon}.$$</tex>

articleTitle: Permutations Fixing a k-set
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i(n,k)$</tex> be the proportion of permutations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi \in \cal {S}_n$</tex> having an invariant set of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>. In this note, we adapt arguments of the second author to prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i(n,k) \asymp k^{-\delta } (1+\log k)^{-3/2}$</tex> uniformly for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\leq k\leq n/2$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta = 1 - {1 + \log \log 2 \over \log 2}$</tex>. As an application, we show that the proportion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi \in \cal {S}_n$</tex> contained in a transitive subgroup not containing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {A}_n$</tex> is at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n^{-\delta +o(1)}$</tex> if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is even.

articleTitle: Examples of Non-trivial Contact Mapping Classes in all Dimensions
abstract: We give examples of contactomorphisms in every dimension that are smoothly isotopic to the identity but that are not contact isotopic to the identity. In fact, we prove the stronger statement that they are not even symplectically pseudo-isotopic to the identity. We also give examples of pairs of contactomorphisms which are smoothly conjugate to each other but not by contactomorphisms.

articleTitle: How Far Can You See in a Forest?
abstract: We address a visibility problem posed by Solomon and Weiss [24]. More precisely, in any dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n:=d+1\ge 2$</tex>, we construct a forest <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {F}$</tex> with finite density satisfying the following condition: if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon \gt 0$</tex> denotes the radius common to all the trees in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {F}$</tex>, then the visibility <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {V}$</tex> therein satisfies the estimate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {V}(\epsilon )= O_{\eta , d}(\epsilon ^{-2d-\eta })$</tex> for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta \gt 0$</tex>, no matter where we stand and what direction we look in. The proof involves Fourier analysis and sharp estimates of exponential sums.

articleTitle: Universal Central Extension of the Lie Algebra of Hamiltonian Vector Fields
abstract: For a connected symplectic manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>, we determine the universal central extension of the Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm ham}(X)$</tex> of hamiltonian vector fields. We classify the central extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm ham}(X)$</tex>, of the Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm sp}(X)$</tex> of symplectic vector fields, of the Poisson Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\infty }(X)$</tex>, and of its compactly supported version <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\infty }_{c}(X)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Rank One Local Systems and Forms of Degree One
abstract: Cohomology support loci of rank one local systems of a smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic variety are finite unions of torsion-translated complex subtori of the character variety of the fundamental group. Tangent spaces of the character variety are (partially) represented by logarithmic 1-forms. In this paper, we give a relation between cohomology support loci and the natural strata of 1-forms given by the dimension of the vanishing locus. This relation generalizes the one for the projective case due to Green and Lazarsfeld and also generalizes the partial relation due to Dimca in the quasi-projective case.

articleTitle: Large Values of Newforms on GL(2) with Highly Ramified Central Character
abstract: We give a lower bound for the sup-norm of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-normalized newform in an irreducible, unitary, cuspidal representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi $</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm GL}_2$</tex> over a number field. When the central character of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi $</tex> is sufficiently ramified, this bound improves upon the trivial bound by a positive power of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N,$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> is the norm of the conductor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi $</tex>. This generalizes a result of Templier, who dealt with the special case when the conductor of the central character equals the conductor of the representation. We also make a conjecture about the true size of the sup-norm in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-aspect that takes into account this central character phenomenon. Our results depend upon some explicit formulas and bounds for the Whittaker newvector over a non-archimedean local field, which may be of independent interest.

articleTitle: Existence of Affine Pavings for Varieties of Partial Flags Associated to Nilpotent Elements
abstract: The flag variety of a complex reductive linear algebraic group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is by definition the quotient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G/B$</tex> by a Borel subgroup. It can be regarded as the set of Borel subalgebras of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Lie}(G)$</tex>. Given a nilpotent element <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Lie}(G)$</tex>, one calls Springer fiber the subvariety formed by the Borel subalgebras which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex> belongs to. Springer fibers have in general a complicated structure (not irreducible, singular). Nevertheless, a theorem by De Concini, Lusztig, and Procesi asserts that when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is classical, a Springer fiber can always be paved by finitely many subvarieties isomorphic to affine spaces. In this paper, we study varieties generalizing the Springer fibers in two ways: being contained in a partial flag variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G/P$</tex> (the quotient by a parabolic subgroup, instead of a Borel subgroup) and defined by a more general belonging condition (in terms of an ideal of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Lie}(P))$</tex>. These varieties arise, for instance, as fibers of resolutions of nilpotent orbit closures. The main result of the paper is a generalization of De Concini, Lusztig, and Procesi's theorem to this context.Communicated by Corrado de Concini

articleTitle: Representations Distinguished by Pairs of Exceptional Representations and a Conjecture of Savin
abstract: We study representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}_n$</tex> appearing as quotients of a tensor of exceptional representations, in the sense of Kazhdan and Patterson. Such representations are called distinguished. We characterize distinguished principal series representations in terms of their inducing data. In particular, we complete the proof of a conjecture of Savin, relating distinguished spherical representations to the image of the tautological lift from a suitable classical group.

articleTitle: Square Functions of Fractional Homogeneity and Wolff Potentials
abstract: In this paper it is shown that, for any measure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBR}}^d$</tex> and for a non-integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 \lt s \lt d$</tex>, the Wolff energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\int\int _0^\infty ({\mu (B(x,r)) \over r^s})^2\,{{\rm d} r \over r}\,{\rm d}\mu (x)$</tex> is comparable to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\int\int_0^\infty\left({\mu(B(x,r)) \over r^s}- {\mu(B(x,2r)) \over (2r)^s}\right)^2\,{{\rm d} r \over r}\,{\rm d}\mu(x),$$</tex> unlike in the case when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex> is an integer. We also study the relation with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-norm of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>-Riesz transforms, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 \lt s \lt 1$</tex>, and we provide a counterexample in the integer case.

articleTitle: Similar Relatively Hyperbolic Actions of a Group
abstract: Let a discrete group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> act by homeomorphisms on compacta <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> with convergence property. Suppose that the actions are minimal that is there is no non-empty proper invariant closed subsets. We will discuss the following question: whether there exist an action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> on a compactum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z$</tex> with convergence property and continuous equivariant maps <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X\leftarrow Z\to Y$</tex>? We call the space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z$</tex> (and action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> on it) pullback space (action). In such general setting, a negative answer follows from a recent result of Baker and Riley (1). Suppose, in addition, that the initial actions are relatively hyperbolic that is they are non-parabolic and the induced action on the distinct pairs are cocompact. In this case, the existence of the pullback space if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is finitely generated follows from (10). The main result of the paper is that the pullback space exists if and only if the maximal parabolic subgroups of one of the actions are dynamically quasiconvex for the other. We provide an example of two relatively hyperbolic actions of the free group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> of countable rank for which the pullback action does not exist. We study an analog of the notion of geodesic flow for relatively hyperbolic groups. Further these results are used to prove the main theorem.

articleTitle: Global Spherically Symmetric Solutions of Non-linear Wave Equations with Null Condition on Extremal Reissner–Nordström Spacetimes
abstract: We study spherically symmetric solutions of semilinear wave equations in the case where the non-linearity satisfies the null condition on extremal Reissner–Nordström black hole spacetimes. We show that solutions that arise from sufficiently small compactly supported smooth data prescribed on a Cauchy hypersurface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde {\Sigma }_0$</tex> crossing the future event horizon <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal H}^{+}$</tex> are globally well posed in the domain of outer communications up to and including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal H}^{+}$</tex>. Our method allows us to close all bootstrap estimates under very weak decay results (compatible with those known for the linear case). Moreover, we establish a certain number of non-decay and blow-up results along the horizon <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal H}^{+}$</tex> which generalize known instability results for the linear case. Our results apply to spherically symmetric wave maps for a wide class of target spaces.

articleTitle: Hankel Determinants, Padé Approximations, and Irrationality Exponents
abstract: The irrationality exponent of an irrational number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi $</tex>, which measures the approximation rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi $</tex> by rationals, is in general extremely difficult to compute explicitly, unless we know the continued fraction expansion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi $</tex>. Results obtained so far are rather fragmentary and often treated case by case. In this work, we shall unify all the known results on the subject by showing that the irrationality exponents of large classes of automatic numbers and Mahler numbers (which are transcendental) are exactly equal to 2. Our classes contain the Thue–Morse–Mahler numbers, the sum of the reciprocals of the Fermat numbers, the regular paperfolding numbers, which have been previously considered, respectively, by Bugeaud, Coons, and Guo, Wu and Wen, but also new classes such as the Stern numbers, and so on. Among other ingredients, our proofs use results on Hankel determinants obtained recently by Han.

articleTitle: Universality for Products of Random Matrices I: Ginibre and Truncated Unitary Cases
abstract: Recently, the joint probability density functions of complex eigenvalues for products of independent complex Ginibre matrices have been explicitly derived as determinantal point processes. We express truncated series coming from the correlation kernels as multivariate integrals with singularity and investigate saddle point method for such a type of integrals. As an application, we prove that the eigenvalue correlation functions have the same scaling limits as those of the single complex Ginibre ensemble, both in the bulk and at the edge of the spectrum. We also prove that the similar results hold true for products of independent truncated unitary matrices.

articleTitle: Structure of One-Phase Free Boundaries in the Plane
abstract: We study classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem in which the free boundary consists of smooth curves and the components of the positive phase are simply connected. We characterize the way in which the curvature of the free boundary can tend to infinity. Indeed, if curvature tends to infinity, then two components of the free boundary are close, and the solution locally resembles an entire solution discovered by Hauswirth, Hélein, and Pacard, whose free boundary has the shape of a double hairpin. Our results are analogous to theorems of Colding and Minicozzi characterizing embedded minimal annuli, and a direct connection between our theorems and theirs can be made using a correspondence due to Traizet.

articleTitle: Large-x Analysis of an Operator-Valued Riemann–Hilbert Problem
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to push forward the theory of operator-valued Riemann–Hilbert problems and demonstrate their effectiveness in respect to the implementation of a non-linear steepest descent method á la Deift–Zhou. In this paper, we demonstrate that the operator-valued Riemann–Hilbert problem arising in the characterization of so-called <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex>-shifted integrable integral operators allows one to extract the large-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> asymptotics of the Fredholm determinant associated with such operators.

articleTitle: Uniform Stability of Twisted Constant Scalar Curvature Kähler Metrics
abstract: We introduce a norm on the space of test configurations, called the minimum norm. We conjecture that uniform K-stability is equivalent to the existence of a constant scalar curvature Kähler metric. This uniformity is analogous to coercivity of the Mabuchi functional. We show that a test configuration has zero minimum norm if and only if it has zero <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-norm, if and only if it is almost trivial.We prove the existence of a twisted constant scalar curvature Kähler metric that implies uniform twisted K-stability with respect to the minimum norm.We give algebro-geometric proofs of uniform K-stability in the general type and Calabi-Yau cases, as well as Fano case under an alpha invariant condition. Our results hold for nearby line bundles, and in the twisted setting.

articleTitle: Gamma Factors of Pairs and a Local Converse Theorem in Families
abstract: We prove a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL(n)\times GL(n-1)$</tex> local converse theorem for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-adic families of smooth representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_n(F)$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> is a finite extension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}_p$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell \neq p$</tex>. Along the way, we extend the theory of Rankin–Selberg integrals, first introduced in Jacquet et al. [20], to the setting of families, continuing previous work of the author [23].

articleTitle: Energy Concentration and A Priori Estimates for B2 and G2 Types of Toda Systems
abstract: For Toda systems with Cartan matrix either <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_2$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_2$</tex>, we prove that the local mass of blowup solutions at its blowup points converges to a finite set. Furthermore, this finite set can be completely determined for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_2$</tex> Toda systems, while for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_2$</tex> systems we need one additional assumption. As an application of the local mass classification we establish a priori estimates for corresponding Toda systems defined on Riemann surfaces.

articleTitle: On the Rationality of the Moduli of Higher Spin Curves in Low Genus
abstract: The global geometry of the moduli spaces of higher spin curves and their birational classification is largely unknown for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g \geq 2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r >2$</tex>. Using quite related geometric constructions, we almost complete the picture of the known results in genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\leq 4$</tex> showing the rationality of the moduli spaces of even and odd 4-spin curves of genus 3, of odd spin curves of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4,$</tex> and of 3-spin curves of genus 4.

articleTitle: Algebraic Independence of Mahler Functions via Radial Asymptotics
abstract: We present a new method for algebraic independence results in the context of Mahler's method. In particular, our method uses the asymptotic behavior of a Mahler function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f(z)$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> goes radially to a root of unity to deduce algebraic independence results about the values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f(z)$</tex> at algebraic numbers. We apply our method to the canonical example of a degree two Mahler function; that is, we apply it to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F(z)$</tex>, the power series solution to the functional equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F(z)-(1+z+z^2)F(z^4)+z^4F(z^{16})=0$</tex>. Specifically, we prove that the functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F(z)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F(z^4)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F'(z)$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F'(z^4)$</tex> are algebraically independent over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}(z)$</tex>. An application of a celebrated result of Ku. Nishioka then allows one to replace <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}(z)$</tex> by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex> when evaluating these functions at a nonzero algebraic number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> in the unit disc.Communicated by Prof. Umberto Zannier

articleTitle: A Spectral Lower Bound for the Divisorial Gonality of Metric Graphs
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> be a compact metric graph, and denote by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta $</tex> the Laplace operator on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> with the first non-trivial eigenvalue <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _1$</tex>. We prove the following Yang–Li–Yau-type inequality on divisorial gonality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma _{{\rm div}}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>. There is a universal (explicit) constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\gamma_{\rm div}(\Gamma) \geq C {\mu(\Gamma) \cdot \ell_{\min}^{{\rm geo}}(\Gamma)\cdot \lambda_1(\Gamma) \over d_{\;\max}},$$</tex> where the volume <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu (\Gamma )$</tex> is the total length of the edges in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell _{\min }^{{\rm geo}}$</tex> is the minimum length of edges in the minimal model of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{\;\max }$</tex> is the largest valency of points of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>. Along the way, we also establish discrete versions of the above inequality concerning finite simple graph models of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> and their spectral gaps.

articleTitle: Formal Symplectic Realizations
abstract: We study the relationship between several constructions of symplectic realizations of a given Poisson manifold. Our main result is a general formula for a formal symplectic realization in the case of an arbitrary Poisson structure on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^n$</tex>. This formula is expressed in terms of rooted trees and elementary differentials, building on the work of Butcher, and the coefficients are shown to be a generalization of Bernoulli numbers appearing in the linear Poisson case. We also show that this realization coincides with a formal version of the original construction of Weinstein, when suitably put in global Darboux form, and with the realization coming from tree-level part of Kontsevich's star product. We provide a simple iterated integral expression for the relevant coefficients and show that they coincide with underlying Kontsevich weights.

articleTitle: Singular Value Statistics of Matrix Products with Truncated Unitary Matrices
abstract: We prove that the squared singular values of a fixed matrix multiplied with a truncation of a Haar distributed unitary matrix are distributed by a polynomial ensemble. This result is applied to a multiplication of a truncated unitary matrix with a random matrix. We show that the structure of polynomial ensembles and of certain Pfaffian ensembles is preserved. Furthermore we derive the joint singular value density of a product of truncated unitary matrices and its corresponding correlation kernel which can be written as a double contour integral. This leads to hard edge scaling limits that also include new finite rank perturbations of the Meijer G-kernels found for products of complex Ginibre random matrices.

articleTitle: On Terminal Fano 3-Folds with 2-Torus Action
abstract: We classify the terminal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBQ}}$</tex>-factorial Fano 3-folds of Picard number one that come with an effective action of a two-dimensional torus. Our approach applies also to higher dimensions and generalizes the correspondence between toric Fano varieties and lattice polytopes: to any Fano variety with a complete intersection Cox ring, we associate its “anticanonical complex,” which is a certain polyhedral complex living in the lattice of one parameter groups of an ambient toric variety. For resolutions constructed via the tropical variety, the lattice points inside the anticanonical complex control the discrepancies. This leads, for example, to simple characterizations of terminality and canonicity.

articleTitle: On Integrability of Discrete Variational Systems: Octahedron Relations
abstract: We elucidate consistency of the so-called corner equations which are elementary building blocks of Euler–Lagrange equations for 2D pluri-Lagrangian problems. We show that their consistency can be derived from the existence of two independent octahedron relations. We give explicit formulas for octahedron relations in terms of corner equations.Communicated by Prof. Igor Krichever

articleTitle: Koszul Gradings on Brauer Algebras
abstract: We show that the Brauer algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm Br}_d(\delta )$</tex> over the complex numbers for an integral parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta $</tex> can be equipped with a grading. In case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta \neq 0,$</tex> it becomes a graded quasi-hereditary algebra which is moreover Morita equivalent to a Koszul algebra. These results are obtained by realizing the Brauer algebra as an idempotent truncation of a certain level two VW-algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vee\!\!\!\!\vee_d^{\mathrm cycl}(N)$</tex> for some large positive integral parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>. The parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta $</tex> appears here in the choice of a cyclotomic quotient. This cyclotomic VW-algebra arises naturally as an endomorphism algebra of a certain projective module in parabolic category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {O}$</tex> of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm D}$</tex>. In particular, the graded decomposition numbers are given by the associated parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials.

articleTitle: Optimal Gradient Estimates for Parabolic Equations in Variable Exponent Spaces
abstract: We establish an optimal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{p(\cdot )}$</tex>-regularity theory for the gradient of weak solutions for parabolic equations in divergence form with bounded measurable coefficients in rough domains beyond the Lipschitz category. With a function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p(\cdot )=p(x,t)$</tex> of spatial and time variables satisfying log-Hölder continuity, we prove that the spatial gradient of the weak solution is as integrable as the nonhomogeneous term in the variable exponent space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{p(\cdot )}$</tex> under the assumption that the coefficients are merely measurable in one of spatial variables while have a small bounded mean oscillation in the other spatial variables and time variable. On the other hand, the domain is assumed to be sufficiently flat in the Reifenberg sense.

articleTitle: On Cohen–Macaulayness of Sn-Invariant Subspace Arrangements
abstract: Given a partition <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>, consider the subspace <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_\lambda $</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBC}}^n$</tex> where the first <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _1$</tex> coordinates are equal, the next <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _2$</tex> coordinates are equal, etc. In this paper, we study subspace arrangements <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_\lambda $</tex> consisting of the union of translates of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_\lambda $</tex> by the symmetric group. In particular, we focus on determining when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_\lambda $</tex> is Cohen–Macaulay (CM). This is inspired by previous work of the third author coming from the study of rational Cherednik algebras and which answers the question positively when all parts of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex> are equal. We show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_\lambda $</tex> is not CM when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex> has at least four distinct parts, and handle a large number of cases when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex> has two or three distinct parts. Along the way, we also settle a conjecture of Sergeev and Veselov about the Cohen–Macaulayness of algebras generated by deformed Newton sums. Our techniques combine classical techniques from commutative algebra and invariant theory; in many cases, we can reduce an infinite family to a finite check which can sometimes be handled by computer algebra.

articleTitle: On Nekovář's Heights, Exceptional Zeros and a Conjecture of Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E/{\BBQ}$</tex> be an elliptic curve which has split multiplicative reduction at a prime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> and whose analytic rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{{\rm an}}(E)$</tex> equals one. The main goal of this article is to relate the second-order derivative of the Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p(E,s)$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> to Nekovář's height pairing evaluated on natural elements arising from the Beilinson–Kato elements. Along the way, we extend a Rubin-style formula of Nekovář to apply in the presence of exceptional zeros. Our height formula allows us, among other things, to compare the order of vanishing of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p(E,s)$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s=1$</tex> with its (complex) analytic rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{{\rm an}}(E)$</tex> assuming the non-triviality of the height pairing. This has consequences toward a conjecture of Mazur, Tate, and Teitelbaum.

articleTitle: Approximation of Sheaves on Algebraic Stacks
abstract: Raynaud–Gruson characterized flat and pure morphisms between affine schemes in terms of projective modules. We give a similar characterization for nonaffine morphisms. As an application, we show that every quasi-coherent sheaf is the union of its finitely generated quasi-coherent subsheaves on any quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic stack.

articleTitle: Lifting Curves Simply
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_\rho (L)$</tex> indicate the smallest integer so that every curve on a fixed hyperbolic surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S,\rho )$</tex> of length at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> lifts to a simple curve on a cover of degree at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_\rho (L)$</tex>. We provide linear lower bounds for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_\rho (L)$</tex>, improving a recent result of Gupta–Kapovich [6]. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S,\rho )$</tex> is without punctures, using work of Patel [9] and Lenzhen–Rafi–Tao [7] we conclude that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_\rho (L)/L$</tex> grows like the reciprocal of the systole of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S,\rho )$</tex>. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S,\rho )$</tex> has a puncture, we obtain lower bounds for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_\rho $</tex> that are exponential in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>.

articleTitle: Wreath Products and Proportions of Periodic Points
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi : \mathbb {P}^1 \longrightarrow \mathbb {P}^1$</tex> be a rational map of degree greater than 1 defined over a number field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> with ring of integers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {o}_k$</tex>. For each prime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {p}$</tex> of good reduction for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi $</tex>, we let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi _\mathfrak {p}$</tex> denote the reduction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi $</tex> modulo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {p}$</tex>. A random map heuristic suggests that for large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {p}$</tex>, the proportion of periodic points of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi _\mathfrak {p}$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {P}^1(\mathfrak {o}_k/\mathfrak {p})$</tex> should be small. We show that this is indeed the case for many rational functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi $</tex>.

articleTitle: Exact WKB Analysis and Cluster Algebras II: Simple Poles, Orbifold Points, and Generalized Cluster Algebras
abstract: This is a continuation of developing mutation theory in exact WKB analysis using the framework of cluster algebras. Here, we study the Schrödinger equation on a compact Riemann surface with turning points of simple-pole type. We show that the orbifold triangulations by Felikson, Shapiro, and Tumarkin provide a natural framework of describing the mutation of Stokes graphs, where simple poles correspond to orbifold points. We then show that under the mutation of Stokes graphs around simple poles the Voros symbols mutate as the variables of generalized cluster algebras introduced by Chekhov and Shapiro.

articleTitle: Noetherian Properties of Fargues-Fontaine Curves
abstract: We establish that the extended Robba rings associated to a perfect nonarchimedean field of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>, which arise in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic Hodge theory as certain completed localizations of the ring of Witt vectors, are strongly noetherian Banach rings; that is, the completed polynomial ring in any number of variables over such a Banach ring is noetherian. This enables Huber's theory of adic spaces to be applied to such rings. We also establish that rational localizations of these rings are principal ideal domains and that étale covers of these rings (in the sense of Huber) are Dedekind domains.

articleTitle: On the Kähler–Ricci Flows Near the Mukai–Umemura 3-Fold
abstract: In this short note, we show that given a special Kähler–Einstein degeneration with bounded geometry, for any noncentral fiber, there exists a Kähler–Ricci flow which converges to the Kähler–Einstein metric of the central fiber. As an example, Tian's deformations [12] of the Mukai 3-fold admit Kähler–Ricci flows which converge to Donaldson's Kähler–Einstein metric [5] over the Mukai 3-fold.

articleTitle: Equivalence Between the Eigenvalue Problem of Non-Commutative Harmonic Oscillators and Existence of Holomorphic Solutions of Heun Differential Equations, Eigenstates Degeneration, and the Rabi Model
abstract: The initial aim of the present paper is to provide a complete description of the eigenvalue problem for the non-commutative harmonic oscillator (NcHO), which is defined by a (two-by-two) matrix-valued self-adjoint parity-preserving ordinary differential operator [28], in terms of Heun's ordinary differential equations, the second-order Fuchsian differential equations with four regular singularities in a complex domain. This description has been achieved for odd eigenfunctions in Ochiai [25] nicely but missing up to now for the even parity, which is more important from the viewpoint of determination of the ground state of the NcHO. As a by-product of this study, examining the monodromy data (characteristic exponents, etc.) of the Heun equation, we prove that the multiplicity of the eigenvalue of the NcHO is at most two. Moreover, we give a condition for the existence of a finite-type eigenfunction (i.e., given by essentially a finite sum of Hermite functions) for the eigenvalue problem and an explicit example of such eigenvalues, from which one finds that doubly degenerate eigenstates of the NcHO actually exist even in the same parity. Also, we determine the possible shape of (so-called) Heun polynomial solutions of the Heun equations, which are obtained by the eigenvalue problem of the NcHO corresponding to finite-type eigenfunctions. Furthermore, as the second purpose of this paper, we discuss a connection between the quantum Rabi model [2, 15, 20, 41] and a certain element of the universal enveloping algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {U}(\Fraktur {sl}_2)$</tex> of the Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {sl}_2$</tex> naturally arising from the NcHO through the oscillator representation. Precisely, an equivalent picture of the quantum Rabi model drawn by a confluent Heun equation is obtained from the Heun operator defined by that element in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {U}(\Fraktur {sl}_2)$</tex> under a (flat picture of non-unitary) principal series representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {sl}_2$</tex> through an appropriate confluent procedure.Communicated by Prof. Eric Opam

articleTitle: Examples of Hyperbolic Hypersurfaces of Low Degree in Projective Spaces
abstract: We construct families of hyperbolic hypersurfaces of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2n$</tex> in the projective space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^n({\BBC})$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\leq n\leq 6$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Classification of Small Linear Functors
abstract: We extend Goodwillie's classification of finitary linear functors to arbitrary small functors. That is we show that every small linear simplicial functor from spectra to pointed simplicial sets is weakly equivalent to a filtered colimit of representable functors represented in cofibrant spectra. Moreover, we present this classification as a Quillen equivalence of the category of small functors from spectra to simplicial sets equipped with the linear model structure and the opposite of the pro-category of spectra with the strict model structure.

articleTitle: Coxeter Groups and their Quotients Arising from Cluster Algebras
abstract: In [1], Barot and Marsh presented an explicit construction of presentation of a finite Weyl group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> by any initial seed of corresponding cluster algebra, that is, by any diagram mutation-equivalent to an orientation of a Dynkin diagram with Weyl group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex>. We obtain similar presentations for all affine Coxeter groups. Furthermore, we generalize the construction to the settings of diagrams arising from unpunctured triangulated surfaces and orbifolds, which leads to presentations of corresponding groups as quotients of numerous distinct Coxeter groups.

articleTitle: Global Analysis of Quasilinear Wave Equations on Asymptotically Kerr-de Sitter Spaces
abstract: We consider quasilinear wave equations on manifolds for which infinity has a structure generalizing that of Kerr-de Sitter space; in particular the trapped geodesics form a normally hyperbolic invariant manifold. We prove the global existence and decay, to constants for the actual wave equation, of solutions.
