The key new ingredient compared with earlier work by the authors in the semilinear case [31] and by the first author in the non-trapping quasilinear case [29] is the use of the Nash–Moser iteration in our framework.

articleTitle: The Global Sections of the Chiral de Rham Complex on a Kummer Surface
abstract: The chiral de Rham complex is a sheaf of vertex algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega ^{{\rm ch}}_M$</tex> on any nonsingular algebraic variety or complex manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>, which contains the ordinary de Rham complex as the weight zero subspace. We show that when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> is a Kummer surface, the algebra of global sections is isomorphic to an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N=4$</tex> superconformal vertex algebra with central charge 6. Previously, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}{\BBP}^n$</tex> was the only manifold where a complete description of the global section algebra was known.

articleTitle: Non-semistable Exceptional Objects in Hereditary Categories
On the Strict Arnold Chord Property and Coisotropic Submanifolds of Complex Projective Space
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\alpha }$</tex> be a contact form on a manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L\subseteq M$</tex> a closed Legendrian submanifold. I prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> intersects some characteristic for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\alpha }$</tex> at least twice if all characteristics are closed and of the same period, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\alpha }$</tex> embeds nicely into the product of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^{2n}$</tex> and an exact symplectic manifold. As an application of the method of proof, the minimal action of a regular closed coisotropic submanifold of complex projective space is at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi /2$</tex>. This yields an obstruction to presymplectic embeddings, and in particular to Lagrangian embeddings.

articleTitle: Variation of Log Canonical Thresholds in Linear Systems
abstract: We investigate the variation of log canonical thresholds in (graded) linear systems. For toric log Fano varieties, we give a sharp lower bound for log canonical thresholds of the anticanonical members in terms of the global minimal log discrepancy.

articleTitle: E-Polynomials of the SL(2, ℂ)-Character Varieties of Surface Groups
abstract: We compute the E-polynomials of the moduli spaces of representations of the fundamental group of a once-punctured surface of any genus into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SL}(2,{\BBC})$</tex>, for any possible holonomy around the puncture. We follow the geometric technique introduced in [12], based on stratifying the space of representations, and on the analysis of the behavior of the E-polynomial under fibrations. Communicated by Prof. Enrico Arbarello

articleTitle: Complexity of Surgery Manifolds and Cheeger–Gromov Invariants
abstract: We present new lower bounds on the complexity of Dehn surgery manifolds of knots, using our recent result on the Cheeger–Gromov <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho $</tex> invariants and triangulations. As an application, we give explicit examples of closed hyperbolic 3-manifolds with fixed first homology for which the gap between the Gromov norm and the complexity is arbitrarily large.

articleTitle: Tau Function Approach to Theta Functions
abstract: We study theta functions of a Riemann surface of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> from the view point of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau $</tex>-function of a hierarchy of soliton equations. We study two kinds of series expansions. One is the Taylor expansion at any point of the theta divisor. We describe the initial term of the expansion by the Schur function corresponding to the partition determined by the gap sequence of a certain flat line bundle. The other is the expansion of the theta function and its certain derivatives in one of the variables on the Abel–Jacobi images of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> points on a Riemann surface with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k\leq g$</tex>. We determine the initial term of the expansion as certain derivatives of the theta function successively. As byproducts, firstly we obtain a refinement of Riemann's singularity theorem. Secondly we determine normalization constants of higher genus sigma functions of a Riemann surface, defined by Korotkin and Shramchenko, such that they become modular invariant.

articleTitle: The Lagrangian Cubic Equation
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> be a closed symplectic manifold and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L \subset M$</tex> a Lagrangian submanifold. Denote by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[L]$</tex> the homology class induced by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> viewed as a class in the quantum homology of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. This paper is concerned with properties and identities involving the class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[L]$</tex> in the quantum homology ring. We also study the relations between these identities and invariants of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> coming from Lagrangian Floer theory. We pay special attention to the case when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> is a Lagrangian sphere.Communicated by Prof. Mohammed Abouzaid

articleTitle: On Beauville's Conjectural Weak Splitting Property
abstract: We investigate Beauville's conjecture on the Chow ring of irreducible symplectic varieties. For special irreducible symplectic varieties, we relate it to a conjecture on the existence of rational Lagrangian fibrations, which proves Beauville's conjecture in many new cases. We further apply the same techniques to reduce Beauville's conjecture to Picard rank two.

articleTitle: Spherically Averaged Maximal Function and Scattering for the Two-Dimensional Cubic Derivative Schrödinger Equation
abstract: We prove scattering for the two-dimensional cubic derivative Schrödinger equation with small data in the critical Besov space with one degree angular regularity. The main new ingredient is that we prove a spherically averaged maximal function estimate for the two-dimensional Schrödinger equation. We also prove a global well-posedness result for the two-dimensional Schrödinger map in the critical Besov space with one degree angular regularity. The key ingredients for the latter results are the spherically averaged maximal function estimate, null form structure observed in [2], as well as the generalized spherically averaged Strichartz estimates obtained in [10] in order to exploit the null form structure.

articleTitle: Arithmetic Correlations Over Large Finite Fields
abstract: The auto-correlations of arithmetic functions, such as the von Mangoldt function, the M<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ddot {{\rm o}}$</tex> bius function, and the divisor function, are the subject of classical problems in analytic number theory. The function field analogs of these problems have recently been resolved in the limit of large finite field size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>. However, in this limit, the correlations disappear: the arithmetic functions become uncorrelated. We compute averages of terms of lower order in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex> which detect correlations. Our results show that there is considerable cancellation in the averaging and have implications for the rate at which correlations disappear when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q \rightarrow \infty $</tex>; in particular, one cannot expect remainder terms that are of the order of the square-root of the main term in this context.

articleTitle: Critical Points of Random Polynomials and Characteristic Polynomials of Random Matrices
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_n$</tex> be the characteristic polynomial of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \times n$</tex> random matrix drawn from one of the compact classical matrix groups. We show that the critical points of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_n$</tex> converge to the uniform distribution on the unit circle as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> tends to infinity. More generally, we show the same limit for a class of random polynomials whose roots lie on the unit circle. Our results extend the work of Pemantle–Rivin [30] and Kabluchko [19] to the setting where the roots are neither independent nor identically distributed.

articleTitle: Counting Cycles in Labeled Graphs: The Nonpositive Immersion Property for One-Relator Groups
abstract: We prove a rank 1 version of the Hanna Neumann Theorem. This shows that every one-relator 2-complex without torsion has the nonpositive immersion property. The proof generalizes to staggered and reducible 2-complexes.

articleTitle: Quantum Serre Theorem as a Duality Between Quantum D-Modules
abstract: We give an interpretation of quantum Serre theorem of Coates and Givental as a duality of twisted quantum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>-modules. This interpretation admits a non-equivariant limit, and we obtain a precise relationship among (1) the quantum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>-module of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> twisted by a convex vector bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> and the Euler class, (2) the quantum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>-module of the total space of the dual bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E^\vee \to X$</tex>, and (3) the quantum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>-module of a submanifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z\subset X$</tex> cut out by a regular section of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> is the anticanonical line bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_X^{-1}$</tex>, we identify these twisted quantum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>-modules with second structure connections with different parameters, which arise as Fourier–Laplace transforms of the quantum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>-module of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. In this case, we show that the duality pairing is identified with Dubrovin's second metric (intersection form).

articleTitle: Upper Bounds for the First Eigenvalue of the Laplacian on Non-Orientable Surfaces
abstract: In 1980, Yang and Yau [20] proved the celebrated upper bound for the first eigenvalue on an orientable surface of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma $</tex>. Later Li and Yau [14] gave a simple proof of this bound by introducing the concept of conformal volume of a Riemannian manifold. In the same paper, they proposed an approach for obtaining a similar estimate for non-orientable surfaces. In the present paper, we formalize their argument and improve the bounds stated in [14].

articleTitle: Affine Grassmannians and Geometric Satake Equivalences
abstract: I extend the ramified geometric Satake equivalence of Zhu [42] from tamely ramified groups to include the case of general connected reductive groups. As a prerequisite, I prove basic results on the geometry of affine flag varieties.

articleTitle: K-Theoretic Characterization of C*-Algebras with Approximately Inner Flip
abstract: It is determined exactly which classifiable C*-algebras have approximately inner flip. The answer includes a number of C*-algebras with torsion in their K-theory, and a number of C*-algebras that are self-absorbing but not strongly self-absorbing.

articleTitle: Symmetries of Hyperbolic 4-Manifolds
abstract: In this paper, for each finite group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, we construct the first explicit examples of non-compact complete finite-volume arithmetic hyperbolic 4-manifolds <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Isom}\,M \cong G$</tex>, or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Isom}^{+}\,M \cong G$</tex>. In order to do so, we use essentially the geometry of Coxeter polytopes in the hyperbolic 4-space, on the one hand, and the combinatorics of simplicial complexes, on the other hand. This allows us to obtain a universal upper bound on the minimal volume of a hyperbolic 4-manifold realizing a given finite group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> as its isometry group in terms of the order of the group. We also obtain asymptotic bounds for the growth rate, with respect to volume, of the number of hyperbolic 4-manifolds having a finite group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> as their isometry group.

articleTitle: Nonharmonic Analysis of Boundary Value Problems
abstract: In this paper, we develop the global symbolic calculus of pseudo-differential operators generated by a boundary value problem for a given (not necessarily self-adjoint or elliptic) differential operator. For this, we also establish elements of a non-self-adjoint distribution theory and the corresponding biorthogonal Fourier analysis. There are no assumptions on the regularity of the boundary which is allowed to have arbitrary singularities. We give applications of the developed analysis to obtain a priori estimates for solutions of boundary value problems that are elliptic within the constructed calculus.

articleTitle: Isometries of Ideal Lattices and Hyperkähler Manifolds
abstract: We prove that there exists a holomorphic symplectic manifold deformation equivalent to the Hilbert scheme of two points on a K3 surface that admits a nonsymplectic automorphism of order 23, which is the maximal possible prime order in this deformation family. The proof uses the theory of ideal lattices in cyclomotic fields.

articleTitle: Degree-2 Abel Maps for Nodal Curves
abstract: We present numerical conditions for the existence of natural degree-2 Abel maps for any given nodal curve. These conditions depend only on the dual graph of the curve. CoCoA scripts were implemented to check these conditions and to return resolutions of the rational degree-2 Abel maps of the curve by means of blowups along Weil divisors. So far, the scripts have verified the validity of the conditions for numerous curves.

articleTitle: Stability and Singularities of Relative Hypersurfaces
abstract: We study relative hypersurfaces over curves, and prove an instability condition for the fibers. This gives an upper bound on the log canonical threshold of the relative hypersurface. We compare these results with the information that can be derived from Nakayama's Zariski decomposition of effective divisors on relative projective bundles.

articleTitle: On a Conjecture of Matsushita
abstract: We prove that Lagrangian fibrations on projective hyper-Kähler <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2n$</tex>-folds with maximal Mumford–Tate group satisfy Matsushita's conjecture, namely the generic rank of the period map for the fibers of such a fibration is either 0 or maximal (i.e., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>). We establish for this a universal property of the Kuga–Satake variety associated to a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex>-type Hodge structure with maximal Mumford–Tate group.

articleTitle: The m/n Pieri rule
abstract: The Pieri rule is an important theorem which explains how the operators <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e_k$</tex> of multiplication by elementary symmetric functions act in the basis of Schur functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s_\lambda $</tex>. In this paper, for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${m \over n} \in {{\BBQ}}$</tex> we study the relationship between the “rational” version of the operators: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$e_k^{{m \over n}} : \Lambda \longrightarrow \Lambda$$</tex> given by the elliptic Hall algebra, and the “rational” version <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s_\lambda ^{{m \over n}}$</tex> of the basis given by the Maulik–Okounkov stable basis construction. The answer is inspired by geometry, but relevant to combinatorics and representation theory.Communicated by Prof. Michael Finkelberg

articleTitle: On the Resolution of Extremal and Constant Scalar Curvature Kähler Orbifolds
abstract: Given a compact Kähler orbifold with an extremal metric, whose singularities admit a local ALE Kähler scalar-flat resolution, we prove that there exists a Kähler desingularization with an extremal metric. Moreover we study the same problem for constant scalar curvature metrics and prove some partial results.

articleTitle: Foliations and Webs Inducing Galois Coverings
abstract: We introduce the notion of Galois holomorphic foliation on the complex projective space as that of foliations whose Gauss map is a Galois covering when restricted to an appropriate Zariski open subset. First, we establish general criteria assuring that a rational map between projective manifolds of the same dimension defines a Galois covering. Then, these criteria are used to give a geometric characterization of Galois foliations in terms of their inflection divisor and their singularities. We also characterize Galois foliations on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^2$</tex> admitting continuous symmetries, obtaining a complete classification of Galois homogeneous foliations.

articleTitle: Global Existence of Small Equivariant Wave Maps on Rotationally Symmetric Manifolds
abstract: We introduce a class of rotationally invariant manifolds, which we call admissible, on which the wave flow satisfies smoothing and Strichartz estimates. We deduce the global existence of equivariant wave maps from admissible manifolds to general targets, for small initial data of critical regularity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^{{n \over 2}}$</tex>. The class of admissible manifolds includes in particular asymptotically flat manifolds and perturbations of real hyperbolic spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBH}^{n}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\ge 3$</tex>.

articleTitle: Correlation Structures, Many-Body Scattering Processes, and the Derivation of the Gross–Pitaevskii Hierarchy
abstract: We consider the dynamics of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> bosons in three dimensions. We assume that the pair interaction is given by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N^{3\beta -1}V(N^{\beta }\cdot )$</tex>. By studying an associated many-body wave operator, we introduce a Bogoliubov–Born–Green–Kirkwood–Yvon (BBGKY) hierarchy which takes into account all of the interparticle singular correlation structures developed by the many-body evolution from the beginning. Assuming energy conditions on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-body wave function, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta \in ( 0,1] $</tex>, we derive the Gross–Pitaevskii hierarchy with 2-body interaction. In particular, we establish that, in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N\rightarrow \infty $</tex> limit, all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-body scattering processes vanish if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k\geqslant 3$</tex> and thus provide a direct answer to a question raised by Erdös et al. [30]. Moreover, this new BBGKY hierarchy shares the limit points with the ordinary BBGKY hierarchy strongly for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta \in ( 0,1) $</tex> and weakly for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta =1$</tex>. Since this new BBGKY hierarchy converts the problem from a two-body estimate to a weaker three-body estimate for which we have the estimates to achieve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta \lt 1$</tex>, it then allows us to prove that all limit points of the ordinary BBGKY hierarchy satisfy the space–time bound conjectured by Klainerman and Machedon [48] for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta \in (0,1)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Pro-p-Iwahori Invariants for SL2 and L-Packets of Hecke Modules
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> be a prime number, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> be a nonarchimedean local field of residual characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>. We explore the interaction between the pro-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-Iwahori–Hecke algebras of the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}_n(F)$</tex> and its derived subgroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SL}_n(F)$</tex>. Using the interplay between these two algebras, we deduce two main results. The first is an equivalence of categories between Hecke modules in characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> over the pro-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-Iwahori–Hecke algebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SL}_2({\BBQ}_p)$</tex> and smooth mod-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SL}_2({\BBQ}_p)$</tex> generated by their pro-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-Iwahori-invariants. The second is a “numerical correspondence” between packets of supersingular Hecke modules in characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> over the pro-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-Iwahori–Hecke algebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SL}_n(F)$</tex>, and irreducible, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional projective Galois representations.

articleTitle: On the Irreducibility of the Space of Genus Zero Stable Log Maps to Wonderful Compactifications
abstract: In this paper, we prove the moduli spaces of genus zero stable log maps to a large class of wonderful compactifications of sober spherical homogeneous spaces are irreducible and unirational.

articleTitle: Twisted Calabi Flow on Riemann Surfaces
abstract: We introduce a twisted version of the Calabi flow. Instead of constant scalar curvature Kähler (cscK) metrics, the twisted version of the Calabi flow is designed to find twisted constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics appearing in the works of Fine [7, 8], Song and Tian [10] and Stoppa [11]. For smooth initial data, we show that on compact Riemann surfaces of positive genus the twisted Calabi flow exists for all times and converges to a solution to the twisted constant scalar curvature Kähler equation under suitable convergence assumptions on the twisting 2-form. Key analytic ingredients are a priori bounds on twisted versions of the energy functionals used by Chruściel [5], Chen [3] and Struwe [13] in their treatment of the Calabi flow on Riemann surfaces.

articleTitle: The Combinatorics of Real Double Hurwitz Numbers with Real Positive Branch Points
abstract: We investigate the combinatorics of real double Hurwitz numbers with real positive branch points using the symmetric group. Our main focus is 2-fold. First, we prove correspondence theorems relating these numbers to counts of tropical real covers and study the structure of real double Hurwitz numbers with the help of the tropical count. Second, we express the numbers as counts of paths in a subgraph of the Cayley graph of the symmetric group. By restricting to real double Hurwitz numbers with real positive branch points, we obtain a concise translation of the counting problem in terms of tuples of elements of the symmetric group that enables us to uncover the beautiful combinatorics of these numbers both in tropical geometry and in the Cayley graph.Communicated by Grigory Mikhalkin

articleTitle: Riemannian Manifolds with Positive Yamabe Invariant and Paneitz Operator
abstract: For a Riemannian manifold with dimension at least 6, we prove that the existence of a conformal metric with positive scalar and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> curvature is equivalent to the positivity of both the Yamabe invariant and the Paneitz operator.

articleTitle: SU(2)-Cyclic Surgeries on Knots
abstract: A surgery on a knot in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^{3}$</tex> is called <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SU}(2)$</tex>-cyclic if it gives a manifold whose fundamental group has no noncyclic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SU}(2)$</tex> representations. Using holonomy perturbations on the Chern–Simons functional, we prove that two <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SU}(2)$</tex>-cyclic surgery coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${p_{1} \over q_{1}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${p_{2} \over q_{2}}$</tex> should satisfy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|p_{1}q_{2}-p_{2}q_{1}|\leq |p_{1}|+|p_{2}|$</tex>. This is an analog of Culler–Gordon–Luecke–Shalen's cyclic surgery theorem.

articleTitle: Common Hypercyclic Vectors for High-Dimensional Families of Operators
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(T_\lambda )_{\lambda \in \Lambda }$</tex> be a family of operators acting on an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>-space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>, where the parameter space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda $</tex> is a subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^d$</tex>. We give sufficient conditions on the family to yield the existence of a vector <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x\in X$</tex> such that, for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda \in \Lambda $</tex>, the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{T_\lambda ^n x;\ n\geq 1\}$</tex> is dense in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. We obtain results valid for any value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq 1$</tex>, whereas the previously known results were restricted to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=1$</tex>. Our methods also shed new light on the one-dimensional case.

articleTitle: On the Logarithmic Green–Griffiths Conjecture
abstract: We establish that for complements of general hypersurfaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H\subset {\BBP}^{n}$</tex> of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geqslant (5n)^{2}\,n^{n}$</tex>, entire holomorphic curves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\colon {\BBC}\to {\BBP}^{n}\setminus H$</tex> are algebraically degenerate. The proof follows in outline the recent implementation by Diverio–Merker–Rousseau of the variational method of Voisin–Siu combined with Demailly's algebraic Morse inequalities, into which it incorporates two new key ingredients, namely an iterated residue formula following Bérczi and low pole order logarithmic slanted vector fields, thereby reducing the reputedly challenging main result to a careful use of majorant series.

articleTitle: Faithful Realizability of Tropical Curves
abstract: We study whether a given tropical curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^n$</tex> can be realized as the tropicalization of an algebraic curve whose non-archimedean skeleton is faithfully represented by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>. We give an affirmative answer to this question for a large class of tropical curves that includes all trivalent tropical curves, but also many tropical curves of higher valence. We then deduce that for every metric graph <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> with rational edge lengths, there exists a smooth algebraic curve in a toric variety whose analytification has skeleton <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, and the corresponding tropicalization is faithful. Our approach is based on a combination of the theory of toric schemes over discrete valuation rings and logarithmically smooth deformation theory, expanding on a framework introduced by Nishinou and Siebert.

articleTitle: Formality of Kapranov's Brackets in Kähler Geometry via Pre-Lie Deformation Theory
abstract: We recover some recent results by Dotsenko, Shadrin, and Vallette on the Deligne groupoid of a pre-Lie algebra, showing that they follow naturally by a pre-Lie variant of the PBW theorem. As an application, we show that Kapranov's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_\infty $</tex> algebra structure on the Dolbeault complex of a Kähler manifold is homotopy abelian and independent on the choice of Kähler metric up to an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_\infty $</tex> isomorphism, making the trivializing homotopy and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_\infty $</tex> isomorphism explicit.

articleTitle: What is the Probability that a Random Integral Quadratic Form in n Variables has an Integral Zero?
abstract: We show that the density of quadratic forms in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> variables over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ}_p$</tex> that are isotropic is a rational function of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>, where the rational function is independent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>, and we determine this rational function explicitly. When real quadratic forms in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> variables are distributed according to the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE) of random matrix theory, we determine explicitly the probability that a random such real quadratic form is isotropic (i.e., indefinite). As a consequence, for each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>, we determine an exact expression for the probability that a random integral quadratic form in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> variables is isotropic (i.e., has a nontrivial zero over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ}$</tex>), when these integral quadratic forms are chosen according to the GOE distribution. In particular, we find an exact expression for the probability that a random integral quaternary quadratic form is isotropic; numerically, this probability of isotropy is approximately 98.3%.

articleTitle: Canonical Projective Embeddings of the Deligne–Lusztig Curves Associated to 2A2, 2B2, and 2G2
abstract: The Deligne–Lusztig varieties associated to the Coxeter classes of the algebraic groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${^{2}A}_2,{^{2}B}_2$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${^{2}G}_2$</tex> are affine algebraic curves. We produce explicit projective models of the closures of these curves. Furthermore for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>, the Coxeter number of these groups, we find polynomials for each of these models that cut out the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBF}_q$</tex>-points, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBF}_{q^d}$</tex>-points, and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBF}_{q^{d+1}}$</tex>-points, and demonstrate a relation satisfied by these polynomials.

articleTitle: The Weinstein Conjecture for Connected Sums
abstract: We prove the Weinstein conjecture for nontrivial contact connected sums under either of two topological conditions: nontrivial fundamental group or torsion-free homology.Communicated by Prof. Simon Donaldson

articleTitle: Crystal Approach to Affine Schubert Calculus
abstract: We apply crystal theory to affine Schubert calculus, Gromov–Witten invariants for the complete flag manifold, and the positroid stratification of the positive Grassmannian. We introduce operators on decompositions of elements in the type-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> affine Weyl group and produce a crystal reflecting the internal structure of the generalized Young modules whose Frobenius image is represented by stable Schubert polynomials. We apply the crystal framework to products of a Schur function with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-Schur function, consequently proving that a subclass of three-point Gromov–Witten invariants of complete flag varieties for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}^n$</tex> enumerate the highest weight elements under these operators. Included in this class are the Schubert structure constants in the (quantum) product of a Schubert polynomial with a Schur function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s_\lambda$</tex> for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|\lambda ^\vee | \lt n$</tex>. Another by-product gives a highest weight formulation for various fusion coefficients of the Verlinde algebra and for the Schubert decomposition of certain positroid classes.

articleTitle: Matrix Dufresne Identities
abstract: We prove a version of the classical Dufresne identity for matrix processes. More specifically, we show that the inverse Wishart laws on the space of positive definite <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r \times r$</tex> matrices can be realized by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \int _0^{\infty } M_s M_s^{\rm T} {\rm d} s$</tex> in which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t \mapsto M_t$</tex> is a drifted Brownian motion on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}_r({\BBR})$</tex>. This solves a problem in the study of spiked random matrix ensembles which served as the original motivation for this result. Various known extensions of the Dufresne identity (and their applications) are also shown to have analogs in this setting. In particular, we identify matrix-valued diffusions built from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_t$</tex> which generalize in a natural way the scalar processes figuring into the geometric Lévy and Pitman theorems of Matsumoto and Yor.Communicated by Prof. Alexei Borodin

articleTitle: Large Deviations for Zeros of Random Polynomials with i.i.d. Exponential Coefficients
abstract: We derive a large deviation principle for the empirical measure of zeros of the random polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_n(z)=\sum _{j=0}^n \xi _j z^j$</tex>, where the coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{\xi _j\}_{j\geq 0}$</tex> form an i.i.d. sequence of exponential random variables.

articleTitle: On Lp-Affine Surface Area and Curvature Measures
abstract: The relationship between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex>-affine surface area and curvature measures is investigated. As a result, a new representation of the existing notion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex>-affine surface area depending only on curvature measures is derived. Direct proofs of the equivalence between this new representation and those previously known are provided. The proofs show that the new representation is, in a sense, “polar” to that of Lutwak's and “dual” to that of Schütt and Werner's.

articleTitle: Removable Singularities of the cscK Metric
abstract: In this paper, we prove a removable singularity theorem for constant scalar curvature Kähler (cscK) metrics, which generalizes the result of Chen–He [3, Theorem 6.2]. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> be a holomorphic function on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBD}^n$</tex> and denote <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S = \{ f=0\}$</tex>. Suppose <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi \in C_{\rm loc}^{\infty }({\BBD}^n {\setminus } S) \cap L^{\infty }({\BBD}^n) \cap PSH({\BBD}^n {\setminus } S)$</tex> defines a cscK metric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$g_\varphi=\sqrt{-1} \varphi_{i \bar{j}}\,{\rm d}z^i\wedge{\rm d}\bar z^j$$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBD}^n {\setminus } S$</tex>. If there exist a constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C \gt 0$</tex> and a function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta (r) = o(1)$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r \rightarrow 0$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${1 \over C} \exp\left\{- \theta\left(|f|\right)|\log|f||^{{1 \over 2}}\right\} I \leq g_{\varphi} \leq C I,$$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I = \sqrt {-1} \delta _{i\bar j} \,\rm d z^i \wedge {\rm d} \bar z^j$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g_{\varphi }$</tex> extends to a smooth cscK metric on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBD}^n$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Degeneration of Moduli of Hitchin Pairs
abstract: In this paper, we prove certain basic results on the construction of a degeneration of the moduli space of Higgs bundles (and more generally Hitchin pairs) on smooth curves, as the smooth curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_{k}$</tex> degenerates to an irreducible nodal curve with a single node. As an application, we get new compactifications of the Picard variety for smooth curves degenerating to irreducible nodal curves.

articleTitle: Sharp Well-Posedness and Ill-Posedness for the Chern–Simons–Dirac System in One Dimension
abstract: We reach completion of separation for the range of Sobolev regularity for well-posedness or ill-posedness of the Cauchy problem for the Chern–Simons–Dirac system in one spatial dimension. We give the answers for the remaining cases from the previous works by Bournaveas et al. [2] and Machihara and Okamoto [19]. The remaining cases correspond to the critical or quasi-super-critical cases from the point of view of scaling. We also extend the previous ill-posed results under the massless setting to the corresponding massive setting.

articleTitle: On Non-Periodic Tilings of the Real Line by a Function
abstract: It is known that a positive, compactly supported function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f \in L^1(\BBR)$</tex> can tile by translations only if the translation set is a finite union of periodic sets. We prove that this is not the case if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> is allowed to have unbounded support. On the other hand, we also show that if the translation set has finite local complexity, then it must be periodic, even if the support of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> is unbounded.

articleTitle: Positive Energy Representations for Locally Finite Split Lie Algebras
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \Fraktur {g}$</tex> be a locally finite split simple complex Lie algebra of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_J$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_J$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_J,$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_J$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \Fraktur {h} \subseteq \Fraktur {g}$</tex> be a splitting Cartan subalgebra. Fix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D \in {\rm der}(\Fraktur {g})$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \Fraktur {h} \subseteq \ker D$</tex> (a diagonal derivation). Then every unitary highest weight representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\rho _\lambda , V^\lambda )$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \Fraktur {g}$</tex> extends to a representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde \rho _\lambda $</tex> of the semidirect product <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \Fraktur {g} \rtimes {\BBC} D$</tex> and we say that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde \rho _\lambda $</tex> is a positive energy representation if the spectrum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-i\widetilde \rho _\lambda (D)$</tex> is bounded from below. In the present note, we characterize all pairs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda ,D)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \lambda $</tex> bounded for which this is the case. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_1(\cal {H})$</tex> is the unitary group of Schatten class 1 on an infinite-dimensional real, complex, or quaternionic Hilbert space and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex> is bounded, then we accordingly obtain a characterization of those highest weight representations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _\lambda $</tex> satisfying the positive energy condition with respect to the continuous <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ {\BBR}$</tex>-action induced by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>. In this context, the representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _\lambda $</tex> is norm continuous and our results imply the remarkable result that, for positive energy representations, adding a suitable inner derivation to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>, we can achieve that the minimal eigenvalue of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde \rho _\lambda (D)$</tex> is 0 (minimal energy condition). The corresponding pairs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda ,D)$</tex> satisfying the minimal energy condition are rather easy to describe explicitly.

articleTitle: Generalized Fourier Transforms Arising from the Enveloping Algebras of 𝔰𝔭(2) and 𝔬𝔰𝔭(1∣2)
abstract: The Howe dual pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Fraktur {sl}(2),O(m))$</tex> allows the characterization of the classical Fourier transform (FT) on the space of rapidly decreasing functions as the exponential of a well-chosen element of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {sl}(2)$</tex> such that the Helmholtz relations are satisfied. In this paper, we first investigate what happens when instead we consider exponentials of elements of the universal enveloping algebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {sl}(2)$</tex>. This leads to a complete class of generalized FTs, that all satisfy properties similar to the classical FT. There is moreover a finite subset of transforms which very closely resemble the FT. We obtain operator exponential expressions for all these transforms by making extensive use of the theory of integer-valued polynomials. We also find a plane wave decomposition of their integral kernel and establish uncertainty principles. In important special cases we even obtain closed formulas for the integral kernels. In the second part of the paper, the same problem is considered for the dual pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Fraktur {osp}(1|2),{\rm Spin}(m))$</tex>, in the context of the Dirac operator on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^m$</tex>. This connects our results with the Clifford-FT studied in previous work.

articleTitle: Topology of Real Milnor Fibrations for Non-Isolated Singularities
abstract: We consider a real analytic map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F = \left (f_1,\ldots ,f_k\right ) : ({\BBR}^n,0) \rightarrow \left ({\BBR}^k,0\right )$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \le k \le n-1$</tex>, that satisfies Milnor's conditions (a) and (b) introduced by D. Massey. This implies that every real analytic map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_I=(f_{i_1},\ldots ,f_{i_l}) : ({\BBR}^n,0) \rightarrow \left ({\BBR}^l,0\right )$</tex>, induced from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> by projections where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \le l \le n-2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I=\{i_1,\ldots ,i_l\}$</tex>, also satisfies Milnor's conditions (a) and (b). We give several relations between the topology of the Milnor fibre of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>, the Milnor fibres of the maps <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_I$</tex>, the link of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F^{-1}(0),$</tex> and the links of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_I^{-1}(0)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Spherical Metrics with Conical Singularities on a 2-Sphere: Angle Constraints
abstract: In this article, we give a criterion for the existence of a metric of curvature 1 on a 2-sphere with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> conical singularities of prescribed angles <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\pi \vartheta _1,\ldots ,2\pi \vartheta _n$</tex> and non-coaxial holonomy. Such a necessary and sufficient condition is expressed in terms of linear inequalities in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vartheta _1,\ldots ,\vartheta _n$</tex>.
